The din was overpowering, just guttural noises to Joao. Around him were inhuman roars, mindless yelling and moaning and chanting. He couldn't think, he could see sound, his head vibrated. "Shut the fuck up!" he yelled impotently at the crowd below him, the sea of fists and cries ceasing not a moment. He couldn't hear his own shout, only feel its vibration in his chest. Perched upon the top of his tank he looked at the line of vehicles ahead, similarly held captive by the oceans around them. All commanders were stuck in similar situations. All facing the same conundrum.

What could he do? Below him were angry eyes, baring teeth, they looked like zoo beasts. He almost felt like throwing them some kind of raw meat. He needed to get through them; the entire convoy did, but how?

He retreated into the tank and closed the hatch, making an effort to shut out at least some of the noise. He yelled to the idling men below him.

"Rotate 90 degrees, slow, we'll force our way through. Watch for my hand signals, remember orders say we can't hit civilians without cause."

He opened the hatch again, returning to the chaos. The tank rotated, slowly. The crowd was forced to shift, but the slow pace avoided panic. He used the pre-prepared hand signals. Slow. Stop.10 degrees more. 20. Full ahead, slow.

They surged backwards. A sudden collision made Joao nearly fall violently, barely holding on. He looked back, the tank having driven into some old wall. Above it were old columns, maybe Roman, one of which had fallen onto some of the poor bastards around him as its support disintegrated. Panic sparked. The shouts turned to screams as frenetic waves smashed into the tank and each other.

options.text: You stupid bastards, you've hit the Temple!" Joao shouted into the tank.

iberiawars_cityfall.20.title: Fall of Faro
iberiawars_cityfall.20.description:
The hum of the engines penetrated the metal of the aircraft, the swirling propellers a transfixing Rodrigo as he stared absently out of his window. The plane was moving onto the runway, hardly a smooth ride as the aircraft swayed and buckled. This thing was junk, a C-201 Alcotan transport. A relic of the old order, they`d had to wheel this thing out of a warehouse and pray it worked.

There were ten passengers, including him. All fellows of the Camara Municipal, the city's now former executive council. None had looked at him and he couldn't blame them since they'd been bundled from their safehouse. Defeat could hardly be laid at his door - he was no military leader - but Faro was his city. The people had been his responsibility, something he had relished as the Republic had been proclaimed.

Seemed all it had led to was slaughter.

They'd been bundled on a plane by soldiers, they didn't even have time to tell them where they were going. There were speculations of fleeing to the Azores. Going to Morocco. Some even said they would be heading North, taking chances with the dangerous airspace. Roderigo leaned into his seat. What'll be will be.

The speed of the aircraft picked up, violently vibrating the passengers. He clutched the armrests of his ancient seat, knuckles white. He had always hated flying.

From ahead of him he heard someone call out. "Hey, what's going on by the fe-"

A chunk of the aircraft disappeared in a flash, shrapnel flying as the plane was thrown violently from its wheels. Roderigo heard the people ahead of him scream before being silenced by the flying shards.The engines ignited into flame as the aircraft disintegrated. They exploded, igniting the fuel lines.

options.text: Before the flame reached him, Roderigo was aware of tanks and soldiers storming through the fence.

iberiawars_cityfall.21.title: Fall of Faro
iberiawars_cityfall.21.description:
The three soldiers sat in silence, watching the pinkish sunlight illuminate the cloud of dust that never seemed to settle. There was a balcony where they could try getting some fresh air, but each worried that it would collapse, the building bearing copious wounds from the battle. Even if they stuck their heads outside, how fresh could the air really be? Faro had fallen, and the streets reeked of burned wood and gunpowder. They were hiding in an apartment that wasn't theirs in a city that no longer welcomed them: an urban limbo.

"We can try for Spain," one of them muttered. "I was forced to learn Spanish as a kid. Might as well use it." He tried to joke. Nobody laughed.

"Out of the frying pan..." Shifting in the armchair which once belonged to a father, the other leaned forward, clasping his hands together. "Going deeper inland is a death sentence. We are already by the sea. Why not get a boat and sail for Morocco?" There was a pause before the man quickly added "or wherever else."

"Do you even know how to sail a ship?" The third man simply lay on the floor, pressing his teeth together to relieve the aching in his spine. "Either they sink us, or we end up starving to death drifting through the Atlantic." He squinted at the flicking chandelier above him. "It's over. Just surrender. We've lost."

The other men's brows furrowed at the suggestion. The soldier in the chair joined the one bound for Spain in searching for a disguise. Scavenging through the apartment, each assembled an outfit that resembled the platonic form of a civilian: ill-fitting shirts, baggy pants, and worn-out shoes that rubbed against their heels. The third just laid there like a piece of broken furniture.

options.text: Instead of saluting, they nodded at each other and left their separate ways.

iberiawars_cityfall.22.title: Fall of Girona
iberiawars_cityfall.22.description:
Silence had fallen over the Plaça de la Independacia, the city having fallen into a grim silence in recent hours as the resistance to the invaders finally ceased. Occasionally a shot would ring out, maybe returned by a volley of cracks, but mostly only a hollow silence reigned.

From his position, Andreu surveyed the square. He had placed himself next to a 4th floor window on the Southern side, the river Onyar on his right and a square entrance blocked with rubble on his left. It was hardly the most secure position, but it was the best he could do. He sat by the window, keeping an eye on the remaining square entrances on the other side.

He had fought for Catalonia for years. He had spread the word of freedom, involving himself in underground politics as much as he could. He had even killed, when he was so ordered - his marksmanship was renowned among those that knew him. But now, the dream was falling apart around him. He hated the silence that reigned over the city.

The sounds of fight had meant it was not the end.

He had thoroughly boobytrapped the buildings. The dirt of the square was already littered with the bodies of some soldiers that had strayed into the area - the others having fled. He had come too far, done too much, to give up now. Besides, this place held symbolic meaning to the Spaniards. The name itself was a monument to when the Bonapartists were driven out. Andreu was confident - they would not destroy this building, and he would not leave.

A grumble from across the square, in the streets close to the entrance, alerted him to newcomers. Some of those that escaped must have got help, a truckload at least by the sound. He shouldered his rifle, and prepared to meet destiny.

options.text: He had no time to think as the armored car entered, and fired its grenade launcher at him.

iberiawars_cityfall.23.title: Fall of Guadalajara
iberiawars_cityfall.23.description:
"My sister was at the Calle de Madrid massacre you fuck" Alvaro heard yelled at him from his fetal position as he tried to protect at least some of his body from the rain of fists and kicks that enveloped him. His body burned and his skin grew more purple. His uniform gained a steadily increasing scarlet stain as half-healed wounds opened and new ones appeared. He begged for mercy, for them to stop, but none came.

"Why should we?" his tormentors questioned. Men and women both laughed and joked between each other as they took their anger out on Alvaro, finding humor in his weeping and begging.

It was over, the city was all but overrun. Alvaro's unit had received an order to withdraw, but it didn't say when or where. They had no radio, and when the man they sent with the runner to the Command Post for clarification never came back. Alvaro didn't wait for his unit to make a decision, he could see where it was going - someone had to survive, and he wasn't going to die for Francoists if he didn't have to.

He had been trying to find clothes to change out of his uniform in apartments when they found him, a small group of citizens riding out the storm - and he'd walked right to them.

Now he was battered on the floor while they decided what to do with him. Moving elicited pain as if his body were filled with knives; he lacked the energy to do much more than moan at the agony. He heard them talk as if he was an observer separated from events.

"Let's just throw him from the window and be done with it, it's a long way down." said the man who had mentioned his sister. Alvaro remembered that day, and could only replay it in his mind as he lay broken.

options.text: He couldn't resist and they lifted him up and moved to the window.

iberiawars_cityfall.24.title: Fall of La Coruna
iberiawars_cityfall.24.description:
The monsters marched through the streets, their long appendages crunching over the rubble on the ground, charred from their fire. The line seemed to never end, cloaked in shadows. They carried guns, the long sticks that boomed endlessly day after day. They knew well the crack it made; they knew to duck.

They watched them from the windows. Some of their friends and people they knew watched in the street despite the late hour. The dark figures chanted words that couldn't be understood, and the people below seemed to not react. However, neither did they. They peered over the window frames, ignoring the shattered glass.

Their parents had said not to worry, the monsters would be gone soon. Promised that soon they could go back to school. They all had similar stories. Dad was a soldier. Maybe Mom worked at the big factory or something. Noone had seen them for some time, and the monsters had come anyway.

For some the food had run out after no one had come home, houses smeared with rotten food and cans they couldn't open. For some monsters had thrown them into the street, said their house was not theirs anymore, and taken it. Some had simply run away when the flying things had made their house collapse, their family missing.

They stared at the creatures down on the street. They all looked the same, and they couldn't see any faces. Just the same horrible bodies, and wherever they went people they knew disappeared. None of them cried. None of them moaned. None said anything at all.

They just gazed at the monsters.

options.text: The monsters didn't look back.

iberiawars_cityfall.25.title: Fall of Leira
iberiawars_cityfall.25.description:
The pungent smell of whatever broth was being prepared under the tarpaulin ahead of them was sickly, a scent new to most of those in the line that stretched back. However, beggars couldn't be choosers, especially when there were men with guns around them.

The ramshackle tent, with a crude chimney cut into its roof emitting smoke, had been placed in a courtyard. Citizens lined up all the way into the street. They clutched whatever receptacle they could, none having been handed out. Cups, bowls, bedpans or just crudely bent metal. Many of them shivered, however there was no cold. Among them murmuring could be heard, voices just loud enough to be audible to the idling guards.

"Line is longer than yesterday."

"Not surprised. Bastards didn't do anything when my block burnt down, they probably burned down another one."

"Anyone know what the slop is today?"

"Shame they wont give us military rations. My husband always said that they were nicer than you thought."

"This isn't military food? Get your husband to try this rubbish."

"I can't, I don't know where he is."

One of the brave souls, a teenager, yelled from the crowd. "Bet your boss eats better than this shit!"

One of the soldiers watching over glared in the direction of the voice. "Any more like that and I'll tip over that broth myself!" he shouted back; the voice didn't come again.

options.text: They all wondered how long they would be allowed to speak so openly.

iberiawars_cityfall.26.title: Fall of Lisbon
iberiawars_cityfall.26.description:
The chain link fence could barely cope with the mass of bodies pushing against it, hordes of desperate souls shouting and pushing against the compound.

It was a small compound, not built to be that defensible. Built in a clearing on the edge of the Monsanto Forest Park, it was little more than a large shack with a fence around it, laden with signs prohibiting trespassers. Half a dozen men stood guard behind the fence, watching the crowd of hundreds anger push towards them.

"Give us the food," they shouted "We can read the signs, we know it's in there, just distribute it!" The metallic ringing of the struggling fence served as a supporting cacophony to their demands.

An officer lifted a megaphone to his lips, his men noting his visible sweat, eyes fixed on the deteriorating barrier. "I`m sorry, I am not authorized to allow distribution of this depot for another two weeks. Please return to your homes."

The response was just more pushing and rage, a harmony of slurs coming from the chaotic mass on their perimeter. Some began to climb the fence. The officer turned to his men.

"Gas masks on, use the tear gas." He pointed at the men climbing over the fence. "Dias, targets are a hundred meters to the front. In your own time, fire."

They carried out the orders mechanically. Seething capsules were fired from launchers into the crowd, earning cries as the white gas attacked the citizens. They broke, scrambling over each other to escape leaving some broken and motionless on the ground. The men who climbed the fence didn't get far, shot nearly as soon as they touched the ground, single shots making them drop like puppets cut from string.

options.text: Incident Report: Crowd dispersed. Minimal casualties.

iberiawars_cityfall.27.title: Fall of Madrid
iberiawars_cityfall.27.description:
The white ceiling was stained with smoke, as the pungent smell of burning filled the building.

The room was long with flickering lights hanging from the ceiling, just one of the many offices that had served the Guardia Civil in more peaceful times. The modern style, smooth walls shuddered from the distant concussions of explosions as men and women dashed around, the concussions often causing a fall, spilling paper onto the gray carpet.

Here, the boring part of keeping the peace had been performed; the record keeping and the administration. Within the records of just this building were the intimate details of a score of the city. Throughout the city, similar offices held information of thousands of 'notable' individuals throughout the country.

The office was bare, the desks chopped and thrown into makeshift bin fires to sustain them. Into the fires people threw every scrap of paper and film they could find - some of them workers, others officers of the force and some citizens who had braved the chaos of the streets to burn records that could incriminate them. All sensed Madrid would soon be unsafe for those who had acted in the interests of Iberia, and none wanted to leave evidence of their conviction.

The fires weren't safe but none cared. They were out of time. Informant information, employee records, operational reports, all had to go. None of them had the time to look whose information was on what document, so the only chance was to burn it all. Nervous hands threw every binder and folder they could into the fires.

From outside, the sounds of gunfire sounded ever closer, a closer explosion earning a worried pause from the burners before they returned to their task. The heat of the room and the tension of time drew a sweat from all of them, streaming into their red eyes.

options.text: The soldiers came and all were gone, but unburned papers remained on the floor.

iberiawars_cityfall.28.title: Fall of Malaga
iberiawars_cityfall.28.description:
Enrique walked out of the building clutching his flag, a shirt tied onto a stick. The reception, its floor coated in broken glass, proved treacherous. Once he stepped outside he longed to return to it.

Before him was a throng of soldiers, along with some vehicles. Even a tank. All were staring at him with violent eyes.

Once, he had been a doctor. When the Republic had been declared, he had become Mayor, in recognition of his democratic agitation. It had limited his career, but he hadn't cared. It was why he became a doctor - he wanted to do what was right, not what made money. Then it had all gone wrong.

As his city had burned and the military took over, he returned to the one place he could make a difference - the city's hospital. Now his beloved Republic was gone, the last soldiers who could walk having fled, and he was tired of death. The hospital was full of those who had suffered too much already. He would do his duty as a doctor first.

He stopped before the soldiers and called out. "Brothers, we surr-"

A crack rang around the air, a bullet hitting one of the soldiers. Enrique was dumbfounded, before processing what happened. He looked back at the hospital and saw a soldier hanging out a window, borderline delirious and barely clutching a pistol, with a nurse trying to drag him back.

"Oh god" he mumbled, before being seized by one of the soldiers. He saw troops taking positions around low walls and vehicles, the turret of the tank ominously pointing towards the hospital's windows.

"No! Don't! Innocent-!" his protests were ended with the butt of a rifle.

options.text: "Direct all fire on enemy building, get the tank to open those walls up."

iberiawars_cityfall.29.title: Fall of Oviedo
iberiawars_cityfall.29.description:
"Maria! Where are you Maria?"

"Keep your head down Juan! Don't look up"

"Papa? We need to move papa please!"

A group of refugees lay as close to the cold pavement of the road as whistling bullets flew overhead. Around them were corpses, some uniformed and some not. Some tried to use the bodies as a shield, others attempted to slowly move to the other side of the street - there a small passage leading away from the gunfight lay, the only window of escape.

They had been trying to stay ahead of the advancing rebels, carefully making their way through a web of apartments to try and stay off the streets. All for naught; the rebels had caught up. Around them were two makeshift defensive lines, held by some of the scant few defenders left. The forward position was barren, the uniformed corpses around them all that remained. The second line, slightly elevated, still resisted with little thought for the people just below their bullets.

Occasionally a stray shot would hit one of the prone figures. Nerves would break and some tried to stand and dash to the passageway, only to be immediately cut down in a crimson cloud. A few made it to the passage, and tried to encourage those still on the road.

A dull rumble sounded at the end of the road, heard even above the cracks of constant gunfire; an armored vehicle coming into view. The refugees that had made it to the passage, at first so determined to stay in sight of their friends and family, all fled, disappearing into the buildings.

Those left on the road heard the powerful gun of the vehicle roar and prayed as it came ever closer.

options.text: The survivors were taken into custody; none spoke a word.

iberiawars_cityfall.30.title: Fall of Pamplona
iberiawars_cityfall.30.description:
Mikel stopped to catch his breath in a grocery store's entranceway, panting but not letting down his guard. He didn't believe he could still run as quickly as he could in his youth but, he reckoned as sweat dripped down his back, mortal danger was a great motivator. The thumps of distant artillery shells rumbled his thoughts, ever calling him to flee.

As the clattering of gunfire slowed down from where he had run, Mikel allowed his shoulders, and then his whole body, to slump to the floor. The street was still, devoid of the bustle of life he was used to. Quiet hung like fog for a moment before rushing footsteps and cries in Basque and Spanish broke the silence of the ghostly street. Mikel closed his eyes, exertion starting to ravage his aged muscles. As stealthily as possible, he peeked around the corner.

Dirty, sunken Basque militiamen were running through the street. Some limped, some carried unmoving bodies. One man, limping with a seeping bloody gash on his right knee, locked eyes with Mikel, but said nothing. There was nothing to be said.

An engine's rumble filled the street as a truck turned in ahead, cramped militiamen huddled on its flatbed. A tattered flag fluttered from its rear, mirroring the state of the men. Most were wounded, a few of them badly, but all still clutched rifles. Mikel turned away and crawled as close to the shop door as he could. Huddling, his thoughts drifted to happier times. The truck's rumble and the soldiers' cries were a grim echo of the thundering bulls and roaring masses who rushed through the street each year. He rocked gently as he pictured the Bull Run, red neckerchiefs symbolising the spilled blood of San Fermin. Then, the parade was one of bloodied masses, screaming as they ran, with a crowd of Spaniards cheering them on. He cried out, the sound unheard as the militiamen passed him by.

options.text: He closed his eyes, praying to San Fermin and any other saint he could remember.

iberiawars_cityfall.31.title: Fall of Pamplona
iberiawars_cityfall.31.description:
They sat by the Magdalena Bridge, laughing and eating around a makeshift fire. They had been ordered to secure the bridge - something that had proved exceptionally easy as the area seemed devoid of any inhabitants. The sounds of battle had continued in the distance but for them, the battle had become purely a spectator sport.

They watched detritus flow down the river past the bridge, at some points a corpse or two.They kept watch on both sides of the Bridge, but it was easy work for the six of them. None came. The nearby convent was empty, with not much of value. It appeared people had been there before they arrived, signs of looting apparent in overturned furniture and broken items littered throughout the disheveled corridors. All they found was some old cans of soup in a pantry.

Now in their third day, they lounged as if no battle was taking place. Perhaps they had been forgotten by their unit? The sounds of battle grew more distant, and they had found enough in the convent to eat for a week. They were not in a hurry.

A boy stumbled up to the group. He was wearing rags, thin with a face lined with dirt. He looked as though he had been living in dirt for some days. He shambled, a desire for speed seemingly matched by fatigue.

"I want to surrender!" he mumbled to the soldiers as he threw up his arms, earning a hearty laugh. He started to shout, trying to match the mocking sound. The soldiers had no interest in taking a prisoner - that would take them from this easy job. Why do that? They picked up stones and discarded cans and began to throw them at the boy.

"Get out of here" they jeered, forcing him to retreat. He cried out to them, asking for some food at least, but they just continued their commands.

options.text: After all, why stop a good thing?

iberiawars_cityfall.32.title: Gifts of Porto
iberiawars_cityfall.32.description:
Ayden moved through the building carefully, hesitating before each door and corner. No one appeared, as his imagination frequently imagined. All he found was corpses and dust.

The building was large but half constructed. Worktables and building materials were strewn all around rooms with indeterminable purpose. The building effort must have been abandoned when the War broke out.

Ayden coughed. He and his team had just been walking by, off to investigate a Golf Course nearby. Being miles from the frontline, they'd assumed safety - then shots had been fired from the construction site they'd been meandering past.

Ayden was all that was left.

Ayden kept investigating, nerves screaming to make sure that it was truly over, when he heard moans from a few rooms away. He fought the urge to run, creeping to the doorway the sound originated from, peering inside. A man in monarchist uniform sat facing the door, his back to the wall. A pool of blood was rapidly extending.

"H...help me" he whispered, his voice gravelly with pain.

Ayden checked they were alone, before walking to him. He checked all around him, thoroughly examining the dying man.

"Thank you" he breathed, looking up at Ayden. As he did, Ayden saw a glint of gold around his neck. Perfect. Ayden grabbed the necklace, pulling it and breaking the chain. He could get something for this.

He stood up, stuffing the necklace into his pocket. It wouldn't bring back any of the rest of his squad, poor bastards, but cash might ease his pain.

options.text: He ignored the pleas of the dying man behind him as he left for home.

iberiawars_cityfall.33.title: Fall of Setubal
iberiawars_cityfall.33.description:
In a different Portugal, Hugo hadn't been an officer. He'd never seen himself in any kind of military role, the idea of being anywhere other than an office going over building plans had been utterly alien to him. An architecture student wanting to make Portugal beautiful, that had been his dream.

Then everything went wrong.

Setubal had been occupied by the decadent Republic, fortunately this monastery had survived the battle quite well, the beautiful Manueline Gothic designs immaculate despite the chaos that had taken the country. The Monastery of Jesus of Setubal had been somewhere he had always wanted to visit when he had been studying in Lisbon - while the circumstances were not ideal, he certainly wasn't going to pass up the opportunity.

He walked around the monastery taking in the shining stone, the white and blue tiling and ornate ceilings filling his fanciful eyes. He took sketches in a little journal he carried, gleefully trying to sketch every detail he could in the limited time he had available. He cursed not having any coloured pencils with him.

Eventually, he walked out. The archway was aged with two separate doors, opening into a large courtyard that was filled with men. To his left and right he could see the roads, mostly empty save for the occasional military vehicle passing through. The men filling the courtyard paid little attention to the historical monument they were next to, standing around makeshift fires cooking and resting. Fools, this place was a jewel before dross.

The idea of ignoring things like they did sickened Hugo, he was thankful that he could appreciate these things. How could they be so ignorant of beauty?

options.text: As he mused, a convoy of trucks laden with political detainees passed by.

iberiawars_cityfall.34.title: Fall of Sevilla
iberiawars_cityfall.34.description:
The air had stopped shaking, and yet had never felt so oppressive.

The fires had been doused and the near explosions had ceased. However, the scars left were everywhere. Building skeletons still barely stood. Blackened arms penetrated out from piles of rubble in the street. Banners declaring their new masters, the only clean things in all the city, flew over the streets.

Survivors picked through the rubble, trying to recover any part of their lives. Most of them followed the commands of the new soldiers without resistance when they were given; there was no resistance left to give. In most streets there was a dull ambience of shifting rubble, stumbling footsteps and the distant hum of trucks.

There was only one place in the city that was truly silent however. Near the river, visible for a long distance thanks to the charred city, was the Seville Cathedral. During the battle it had been a sanctuary where the grace of God had been said to protect all from the horror of the city.

Now, it's a dark joke against that grace. Bulging eyes watched the city, their city, from the Giralda. Before they had been members of the new democratic administration of the city. Now, suspended with rope, they lined the perimeter of the tower. Their skin, battered and bruised, was degrading fast as it was exposed to the elements. They wore nothing but a sign around their necks. The sign declared each man and woman there as an enemy of the new Spain.

It called them degenerate Jew lovers.

It called them tyrannical cowards

It called them traitors.

options.text: They had all believed in a brighter future once.

iberiawars_cityfall.35.title: Fall of Valencia
iberiawars_cityfall.35.description:
A group of Republican soldiers absently gazed at the road before them. They were sitting in rows, cross legged on the side of a road junction. The buildings around were burned down, however the fires and explosions had failed to collapse the area so the shells still stood. Around them were guards, absently meandering around in a bid to kill time. The captives had no such luxury.

Soldiers were marching along the road, with the occasional vehicle and a surprising amount of horse drawn equipment. There was somewhat of an air of disorganization if one looked. Officers unfamiliar with the city even before half had been reduced to rubble struggled to make sense of maps while their men were forced to wait across the road from the captives who had recently been trying to kill them. Trucks sometimes forced their way through marching columns with a blaring horn, earning a slew of insults and the occasionally thrown rock. It was all enough to get a bitter chuckle from some of the captives.

One of them however was staring a little way down the road. There, inscribed on the wall of a building on the opposite side of a turning, was an advert for a local family Paella restaurant. Much of the color and definition had faded thanks to the violence that surrounded it but the basic mural remained.

There was a smiling face, though age or sex couldn't be made out, with a pan of steaming paella painted next to it. Below was the blotched name of the restaurant. Maybe there had once been an arrow, or a location listed, but it had since been worn away likely due to the City's considerable current struggle.

The soldier's stomach grumbled. He hadn't eaten in two days, and he was unsure when the next meal would come. A barked order to stand drew his attention away from his object of longing however, and within minutes the captives were marching down the street again.

options.text: War has its most common deprivations.

iberiawars_cityfall.36.title: Fall of Valladolid
iberiawars_cityfall.36.description:
The air, thick with dust, choked Hugo as he lay on the ground. His body burned in agony, his clothes and skin ripped away around him as he hung his mouth open, silently screaming. The dust, broken brick and blood all vyed to cover his wounds in a putrid display.

Moments ago he and some others had been standing proud, defending a house against the incoming onslaught of rebels to the city. They'd been cut off from the retreat and their young hearts had decided upon a glorious last stand, none of them older than 20. They'd opened fire on the first patrol they had seen, basking in a glow of pride as they cut down a score of men forcing the patrol to flee.

The tank that soon turned the corner, fired its gun and collapsed the front of the building took that feeling away.

Hugo didn't know where the others were, maybe they were in the drift of rubble that he was a part of? Maybe they had fled? As Hugo tried to stand the thoughts were quickly lost in a sea of blinding mental fire. His legs twisted in strange ways, his right arm had skin hanging from it from where he had been dragged across the rubble as he'd fallen. He realized he could only see from one eye, and the pool of blood grew. He remained on the street paving, half shrouded by rubble, unable to move as every motion sent further jolts of pain.

The dust steadily began to settle, forming a blanket atop him. He heard dull groans from behind him as his mind began to fade, the pain disappearing slowly but steadily into an overwhelming numbness. Through the sullen cloud he became dimly aware of advancing figures, silhouettes he could barely focus on as he felt strangely unable to register his vision.

Soon, the dark figures saw him and approached. He didn't hear the shot that followed.

options.text: Private Hugo Guzman, 19 years old, MIA.

iberiawars_cityfall.37.title: Fall of Vigo
iberiawars_cityfall.37.description:
The office was a mess, files and furniture torn all around. It shared the same fate as the factory to which it was attached. Machines destroyed, blasted into pieces and strewn around the assembly floor. The bombs and gunfire had done their work.

Now it lay quiet, a liminal silence hanging from the atmosphere.

In the office the silence took on a different character. A safe that had been concealed behind a painting was revealed. It had taken some effort, but it now hung open with its contents bare to the group of soldiers that stared in awe at it. There were over a dozen of them packed into the office, all crowded around their prize.

"That's a lot of cash," one muttered. The safe was stuffed, nearly bursting with the prized notes.

"Must be wages. These factories were going right until the end, those workers wouldn't stick around without their cash ready" another said.

"Is it some Galician currency? That stuffs worthless."

One of them stepped forwards and dug around the safe's contents. "Nope. Peseta."

A rapacious cheer rose from the soldiers, ringing across the factory. They enthusiastically started distributing their spoils between each other, dreaming of its use. Some talked of saving, others vices. Some just counted their share with glee.

options.text: As they left they stepped over the body in the doorway, the blood on his shirt still wet.

iberiawars_cityfall.38.title: Fall of Zaragoza
iberiawars_cityfall.38.description:
None of them resisted as they were dragged into the street, out of the basement they had been thrown into days before. Most of them could barely stand anyway.

The street was relatively empty, but a few citizens were slowly moving past the building, an otherwise nondescript house in Zaragoza which had been conspicuously guarded by a squad of soldiers for a few days, a guard outside the door rotating every few hours. A few local residents had seen this but none asked why.

The soldiers pushed the bloodied prisoners up against the wall of the building. Some of them immediately slumped down, sitting like a doll. Others just about retained their feet, leaned up against the wall. Some coughed. Some wept. Some just spat blood and were silent. All had countless bruises and cuts, blood tried into their rags - their treatment was clear.

After they were satisfied with their prisoners, they began to stop passersby and residents in nearby houses, creating a tiny crowd of a dozen or so.

"These men and women," the soldiers' leader declared, "are guilty of working with the Iberian regime, of oppressing the spirit of Spain for their own petty power-"

"We're office workers, that's all we are, we swear!" one of the prisoners meekly professed, interrupting the speech. The leader barked an order, one of his men punching the prisoner. Their head struck the brick wall behind them, drawing blood as they numbly slid down.

"Citizens of Zaragoza, witness our commitment to your liberation. The Francoists will oppress us no more". With that, the soldiers turned and shouldered their rifles.

options.text: Within moments, the murder was completed.

iberiawars_cityfall.39.title: Liberation of Aveiro
iberiawars_cityfall.39.description:
They came for Afonso as night fell. Armed men, some dressed in Republican uniforms with crude red armbands and some simply in civilian clothes, hauled him from his seminary and practically threw him into the back of a truck. He recognised many of those he saw, fellow priests from the city, packed tight. There was barely enough room to breathe.

The truck drove for what felt like an eternity. Hardly anyone spoke a word. Some were dazed, a few bruised. Others simply closed their eyes, whether in sleep or contemplation Afonso couldn't tell. Night fell as they drove, a caustic blackness surrounding them all. There were no more lamplights.

Eventually the truck came to a stop, the armed men ordering the priests to get out. Other trucks hummed around a clearing, their lights illuminating the darkness. Poor souls disembarked from them. Shaken, Afonso couldn't gather a headcount, all thoughts banished in favor of a raw terror as he realized what they were being marched towards.

A large ditch had been dug, a hellish crevice moaning with those already within. A few froze in terror - they were dealt with instantly to the horror of the captives. Regrets invaded Afonso. Why hadn't he fled? What use had he hoped to serve to his flock? What had been the point? He began panting, his chest tight and mind racing as he crept ever closer to the abyss.

They jumped in, fear controlling them. They were crammed together and the socialists began to line up along the edge of the ditch, silhouettes against the headlamps. Jostling against those next to him, Afonso clasped his hands. Perhaps he would be missed. Perhaps he could hide and survive. Vain hopes danced in his head as they did all the others in the pit. Their executioners raised their rifles, and Afonso offered a simple prayer.

options.text: God... save us from this madness.

iberiawars_cityfall.40.title: Liberation of Badajoz
iberiawars_cityfall.40.description:
TOP SECRET

COMMUNIQUE TO THE WAR MINISTER: FOR IMMEDIATE ATTENTION

Sir,

Badajoz has been secured. Organized resistance removed from the immediate vicinity of the city. City saw a heavy amount of street fighting. Early attempts to employ indirect fire strategies ineffective. Partisan activity prevented artillery stores being adequately replenished. Close quarters fighting has left much of the city uninhabited.

Higher than expected civilian deaths recorded. Civilians often trapped by rebels close to combat. Lower than expected resistance to martial law is being observed as a result. Guerilla raids continue in the immediate vicinity. Supply lines unstable. Much of the civilian population fled south or into Portugal.

Prisoners will be transferred. Recommend authorization to relocate surrendered citizens unsuitable for labor to monitored camps deeper behind the lines. Unsurrendered citizens who refuse relocation are not being aided. Limited supplies amid fears of counterattack reduce scope of current operations.

General Fernando Cabrera, Head of Military Security District Center.

options.text: The shields of the rebels shall fall with them; those that remain shall work.

iberiawars_cityfall.41.title: Liberation of Barcelona
iberiawars_cityfall.41.description:
TOP SECRET

COMMUNIQUE TO THE WAR MINISTER: FOR IMMEDIATE ATTENTION

Sir

Barcelona can be considered under our control as the Military Administration has taken control of all operations within the city. The situation can be considered stable, however there does remain a variety of issues which security forces are attempting to rectify.

1: There remains a high amount of nationalist dissidents within the population. Any publicly espousing such views are being identified and detained where possible. Current resources make this unsustainable, as such I recommend relocation of offenders to camps elsewhere

2: There remains a high terrorist presence both in the city and the surrounding area. Patrols of main routes are being prioritized as forces are insufficient to cover non essential routes and locations.Punitive actions and intelligence are still being considered.

3: Some remnants of the defending army remain in cultural locations. For some indirect siege tactics are being employed, others rapid assault, depending on the risk of damage to cultural monuments.

It can be said that this city is still at war with us, even if the rebel army has been displaced. Further information will be forwarded as soon as intelligence gathering has been concluded.

General Carlos Fernandez, Head of Military Security District Catalonia.

options.text: A map changes easier than a soul.

iberiawars_cityfall.42.title: Liberation of Bilbao
iberiawars_cityfall.42.description:
TOP SECRET

COMMUNIQUE TO THE WAR MINISTER: FOR IMMEDIATE ATTENTION

Sir

Bilbao razed. Large areas of Bilbao unfit for habitation. Disease concerns within inner city. Socialist terrorists still active in region. High sympathy for dissidents in region. Most local infrastructure damaged or destroyed.

Actions Taken: Mass arrests, martial law and emergency sentencing carried out. Incentives for cooperation with security forces offered with some success. Relocation of citizens from uninhabitable districts ongoing. Anti-terrorism operations ongoing.

Concerns: Limited local cooperation. Civilian camp conditions degrading. Despite high expense local terrorism continues with moderate impact on operations. Insufficient means to begin reconstruction.

Request: Reconstruction Report be compiled and published. Material for 2 major civilian camp constructions. Further anti-terrorism experts be dispatched to advise operations. More details to follow in report.

General Emilio Huesca, Head of Military Security District Basque-Navarre.

options.text: The lion's den was razed, yet it stays on the hunt.

iberiawars_cityfall.43.title: Liberation of Cadiz
iberiawars_cityfall.43.description:
TOP SECRET

COMMUNIQUE TO THE WAR MINISTER: FOR IMMEDIATE ATTENTION

Sir,

Cadiz and its surrounding regions have been successfully transferred to the MSD. The result of the shock tactics employed with sole regard to hostile positions, and the eradication of boats trying to leave in the final moments of the battle, has resulted in a passively resistant population which may risk turning violent once more without reinforcement. Damage to the city is moderate with damage majoritively in the dense areas and docks. The Cadiz docklands can not be repaired with current resources. Security forces are spread thin as terrorism continues within the city.

Efforts have been taken to trace the production sites of literature and posters slandering our forces as engaging in acts of massacres against refugees. Suspects in the spread of such misinformation have been detained and are currently being interrogated.

Full suppression is difficult with current means and more units are requested urgently. Further engineers and tools to equip laborers to repair the docks, as laid out in the memorandum received last month as a priority objective should they be damaged, are also requested.

General Luis Delgado, Head of Military Security District South

options.text: They will be made to see; only the guilty flee.

iberiawars_cityfall.44.title: Liberation of Cartagena
iberiawars_cityfall.44.description:
TOP SECRET

COMMUNIQUE TO THE WAR MINISTER: FOR IMMEDIATE ATTENTION

Sir,

Cartagena's placement under martial law has been simultaneously simpler and more complex than other areas in Military District East.

The military campaign that took Cartagena utilized significant force in reaction to a high concentration of rebel forces. Destruction was regrettably high, however it seems that the dispersal of terrorist cells in the region was rather more effective as a result. Local groups seem to have retreated elsewhere or been destroyed. The cost of this however is the difficulty in local administration and policing that such destruction is causing.The area surrounding the city has become a patchwork of settlements due to the danger of civilian movement. Easing the Civilian humanitarian situation in order to limit impacts on the military are limited by the difficulty in movement caused by the loss of infrastructure.

Morale among citizens identifiably hostile to our administration appears low, with the desire for further anti-government action minimal. Banditry is prevalent, however they do not seem to target military movements. The few that have are swiftly destroyed, observed to be civilians armed only with salvaged small arms often. Efforts to corral at-risk populations into monitoring camps and patrolling vital routes has guaranteed that there is minimal risk of banditry to military movements. Further Engineering corps units will be required to make significant progress in the rebuilding of vital infrastructure.

General Carlos Costa, Head of Military Security District East.

options.text: We will do all we can, within the bounds of practical military necessity.

iberiawars_cityfall.45.title: Liberation of Coimbra
iberiawars_cityfall.45.description:
For the Attention of the Council of Ministers,

Gentleman,

Monarchists have been expelled from the City of Coimbra, and with it one of the first lines of defense that were set up by their forces finally breached. Due to its proximity to initial contact lines it appears that the illegal administration did not invest in substantial fortifications inside the city. However, an easy campaign was not offered by this, as a mass mobilization and liberal use of ambushes and explosives saw heavy losses in all involved parties, civilian and military.

Most Infrastructure, at least 20% of the city's buildings and local logistical hubs have been destroyed, with many more of the buildings in the vicinity of combat encounters are structurally unsound or damaged beyond safe use. Food, water and medicine supplies left behind by monarchists have not been found intact, many of the depots destroyed as our forces approached.

Heavy losses among our troops and the catastrophic destruction of much of the area's infrastructure, further frustrated by terrorist groups continuing to operate past the withdrawal of most monarchist units, the area has already been declared a zone of humanitarian disaster. Initial efforts to redirect aid have been conducted by the military however a comprehensive response will require further planning. In the meantime, local units have been instructed to only distribute food marked for civilian distribution in order to avoid frustrating the logistics of our own troops any more than necessary. Recommendations for a response will be discussed at the next meeting.

Signed,

Defence Minister Gomes

options.text: The weaponization of the city itself was a crime against its people.

iberiawars_cityfall.46.title: Liberation of Coimbra
iberiawars_cityfall.46.description:
No one had seen the list nailed to the door of the Church, hanging like a vine from the aged wood. It had appeared overnight before the Sunday Mass, and now the congregation laid their eyes upon it and stood silently in vigil.

The list was perhaps a metre long, at the top loudly emblazoned with a simple message and a hammer and sickle. "These individuals are suspected of counter-revolutionary allegiances," it said in stark red letters, "and so are wanted for public protection. Any information leading to the arrest of enemies of the People will be remembered and rewarded with official recognition that the individual is an ally of the Revolution." Below were names of dozens and dozens, falling to the ground.

It was a small Church, serving a small community located in some hills near Coimbra. They'd wanted only to be left alone; for years God granted them that wish. The concerns of Iberia passed them by. A King had returned and they'd seen hope, their Padre telling them of how a more godly Portugal awaited. Then the socialists came and for the first time since Napoleon they had seen soldiers. They'd left again, but stories from neighbouring towns trickled. The beatings. The disappearances. The broken corpses found in the streets, draped in red. They still dared to come to Mass, no one had come to outlaw it yet, but if they came once they could come again.

For the first time since Napoleon, fear hung in their hearts.

"Sorry I'm late!" came a shout from behind the group. "My door got jammed somehow, nearly had to -" The Padre appeared, passing through the motionless crowd before seeing the list. His congregation remained silent as he read it, looking down the names.

He saw his own. His skin burned as he felt the eyes looking at him.

options.text: In a small office, a small man grinned. The reports were good, and the small cells were full.

iberiawars_cityfall.47.title: Liberation of Cordoba
iberiawars_cityfall.47.description:
TOP SECRET

COMMUNIQUE TO THE WAR MINISTER: FOR IMMEDIATE ATTENTION

Sir,

Consolidation of Cordoba is ongoing as the final arrangements for the transfer to security forces are made. The breaching of the city was achieved with a rapid breakthrough of the frontline after the city was encircled. Resistance was quickly crushed. Some military units were able to break through the weaker part of the lines but most refugee and enemy routes out of the city were successfully neutralized.

As a result of the rapid assault operation we have received a number of detained city officials appointed by the rebel occupiers. They have been detained with assessments ongoing as to their value. Limited manpower restricts our ability to maintain adequate prisoner guarding, as such any defined as low-value will be liquidated.

Protests have occurred against our forces by remnant Republicans. Leaders have been detained, however we are short on riot equipment. Request riot gear and rubber bullets, without it we will be forced to employ lethal methods as standard policy. Guerilla raids are harsh in the surrounding area, vital routes have frequent patrols however inadequate resources are leading to less significant areas suffering banditry. While not militarily damaging and as such not high priority, ignoring this issue could undermine our position long term. More manpower is required to police these regions effectively.

General Luis Delgado, Head of Military Security District South.

options.text: We shall cleanse the city as efficiently as we took it.

iberiawars_cityfall.48.title: Liberation of Evora
iberiawars_cityfall.48.description:
For the eyes of the King: Notification regarding the successful liberation of Evora.

Sire,

Regrettably, while Evora has now been secured against continued organized resistance to our forces, I cannot report to you that the city is at peace. The assault extracted a high price from the city, resulting in the damage or destruction of large areas, notably some of its distinctive architecture. Further, it has been informed to me that the city remains unstable with a hostile population frequently acting against our security forces.

Instances of protest remain frequent. Currently we are trying to limit hostile actions against dissidents for fear of escalating the situation, however our security forces are stretched thin. Further the situation seems to be resolving at a slow pace, pressing our forces further. Hopes that the difficult humanitarian situation, which while not catastrophic is certainly present with food and medical supplies scarce in some areas, would naturally calm the protests have been proven unfounded.

Aside from protests, terrorist attacks remain frequent, something that has been complicated by the aggressive population. While their attacks fail to fatally affect operations in the area they act as a constant draw on our resources.

However, let me state that this does not take away from the achievement of your armed forces. Despite the odds they took and continue to hold one of Portugal's key cities. 

God Save the King

Defence Minister Fernando dos Santos Costa

options.text: Righteousness begets struggle, struggle begets Victory.

iberiawars_cityfall.49.title: Liberation of Evora
iberiawars_cityfall.49.description:
"Why do you make me do this?"

The room was bright, the blue sky outside allowing in glistening sunlight. It illuminated a wretched shape tied to a central table with their limbs outstretched. Bloodied and broken, they wept openly, fueled by the putrid stench of the room and the grievous wounds upon their body. Their arms and legs were bent at perverse angles, shards of bone piercing the skin. Discarded lay a blooded bat.

A man looked outside, admiring the day while fitting a belt. "I'm not a monster, friend. I enjoy many of the things you do. A nice place to work. A warm day. A drink in the evening." He turned and walked to his snivelling subject, displaying the belt of surgical tools he wore.

"If you tell me where the rest of your resistance cell is, my job is done. We can talk about something far more civil." He smiled warmly. "If you people didn't persist in your folly, this wouldn't be necessary. I'd much prefer to meet as friends than rivals. After all, aren't we both subjects of the King?"

"I'm not part... of any cell... I don't know... Please..." came the strained hesitant reply.

The Man sighed, drawing a scalpel from his belt. It was long and slightly curved at its end, still dripping from the alcohol it had been soaking in prior.

"I am truly sorry brother, but if we have to continue this unpleasantness so be it. It's your choice." Soft, squishy tearing cried around the room, a sickening sound barely masked by the scream that accompanied it.

"Where are your friends?" said the Smiling Man.

options.text: "I would love to meet them."

iberiawars_cityfall.50.title: Liberation of Evora
iberiawars_cityfall.50.description:
"Great job, you idiot!" The staging point's leader jabbed his finger at the tank. "Do you realize how old that temple was?" In response, Gaspar made a visceral sound he didn't quite know the meaning of, looking between his other crewmates. The loader was cautiously understanding while the assistant driver looked up at the sky, maybe hoping that God would scoop him up to heaven for a few minutes. His commander—a younger man whose vocal cords had been obliterated by all the shouting he did in the cockpit—was eerily silent for once.

"Sir, there were protesters all around us. They had the whole street locked down." Gaspar spoke up, remembering the inadvertent crunching of the Roman stone under the treads of his tank as he'd attempted to maneuver.

"The protestors." The leader's voice was like a hyena's yelp: sharp and mocking. "Joao, who do you think history will remember when this war is over? You want to live long enough to see that happen, right?"

"Yes sir."

"So who will they remember: a few enemies of the revolution? Or the cultural vandals?" Gaspar felt a strand of sweat sliding down the nape of his neck, yet he dared not raise a hand to swipe it away. Now, it was time for the staging point's leader to make the same few visceral sounds. He looked down at his watch and sighed.

options.text: "Dismissed. Use some common sense in the future."

iberiawars_cityfall.51.title: Liberation of Faro
iberiawars_cityfall.51.description:
For the eyes of the King: Notification regarding the successful liberation of Faro.

Sire,

It is my pleasure to announce that Faro has been seized from the usurpers through a rapid assault. Cessation of local hostilities has been largely achieved, and I have received reports that the rapid expulsion of republicans from the city has been a major success in our Algarve operations.

The city, with its location on the Gulf of Cadiz, represented a major republican stronghold in Southern Portugal. Our forces therefore contained the city, forming a perimeter around it and resisting attempts to break the encirclement, before staging a shock offensive with the use of mechanized units and storming units. Coordination between aerial, artillery and mobile units restricted any attempts to resist. Of note, forward units were able to seize the airport and prevent the evacuation of a variety of significant republican figures. Those who were seized alive are being relocated North for further interrogation.

Effects on the civilian population have been significant, with attempts at fleeing blocked to prevent complicating local logistics any more than they already are. Those whose homes are uninhabitable are being distributed to accommodations conducive to local operations.

Terrorism persists in the area, particularly among former left wing military units and sympathizers. Plans to expand our counter-terrorism operations in the area are being compiled presently and I hope that our citizens can have peace restored as soon as possible.

God Save the King

Defence Minister Fernando dos Santos Costa

options.text: Our Majesty shall shine to all corners of our land.

iberiawars_cityfall.52.title: Liberation of Faro
iberiawars_cityfall.52.description:
War had not been as young recruit Beto had imagined it. Yes, there was glory for those looking at the great maps. For his platoon, it had been a drudging, deadly boredom.

Recent weeks had been little but standing sentry and the occasional patrol where nothing happened, but a tantalizing sense of finality rushed through him as he and his comrades broke the pithy resistance of the Faro Airport defenses. With a roar, he was first through the breach and charged towards the escaping plane their tank had struck, smiling. Final, scattered gunshots sounded as the final efforts at defense were made, but most were fleeing across the tarmac. He would be the first to claim any survivors as prisoners. That, at least, was his.

The smell of the burning plane wreck was repulsive. Beto saw a twisting mass amongst the flickering flames and, bracing himself against a smoldering chair, it took several moments to realize the thing was human. Amongst the debris and oozing once-peoples, it stared at him with unblinking eyes. It tried to reach out, even stand, only half-aware of its fate. With pure agony, the arm was raised, before dropping along with a dollop of sloughed-off flesh.

"Help..." It twisted with the motions of Beto's guts, a voice as charred as the corpse before him, "I didn't want to. Please... ho- home, take me! Now! I'm your Mayor. Me, Roderigo! Mama... save me..." Its rasp concluded and energy spent, it slumped, muttering.

Wide-eyed, Beto silently walked away. Further and further he retreated, but the horror he felt only built. Even keeling over to puke did not stop the assault on his senses. Looking back, he saw his squad following him in abandoning the wreck, pursued by more than the stench.

options.text: The continuing battle called them from across the tarmac, and they fled towards it.

iberiawars_cityfall.53.title: Liberation of Guadalajara
iberiawars_cityfall.53.description:
Communique to the Office of the President of the Spanish Republic

Sir,

Guadalajara has been taken with the final hostile units withdrawing from the city. Our flag flies over the city and citizens are beginning to greet our units. Currently great caution is being exercised due to the potential for attacks from still-hidden isolated units or Nationalist aligned terrorists.

The city has been able to avoid substantial damage in the central areas, with most of the harsher fighting confined to the residential areas on the outskirts. A threat of encirclement thanks to a breakthrough of our forces on the Western side of the city forced a choice between withdrawal or a siege; it appears the defenders chose an ordered withdrawal.

Something that likely precipitated this choice was the high degree of civilian resistance to the troops within the city. There is evidently a high degree of enthusiasm for regime change within the city. We have testimony of multiple small uprisings in the enemy rear, of which some were successful in securing entire city areas.

Disturbingly, some isolated Falange aligned troops who remained in the city began to employ civilians as mobilized soldiers. While confrontations against such groups were limited, they prompted some instances of violence. Care is being taken to shield journalists from those violent situations, however instances where civilians surrendered will be used in reports.

Press Releases are being prepared. Guidelines for broadcasting the stories relating to the uprisings are being prepared, with appropriate interviewees being screened. With the right portrayal we can turn Guadalajara into a model for future urban offensives.

options.text: We shall give the people an example to follow.

iberiawars_cityfall.54.title: Liberation of La Coruña
iberiawars_cityfall.54.description:
TOP SECRET

COMMUNIQUE TO THE WAR MINISTER: FOR IMMEDIATE ATTENTION

Sir

La Coruna's administration has now been successfully transferred to the Military Security District. Fortunately, resistance appears to be manageable with terrorism present, but tolerable, with appropriate measures being carried out by security forces. Intelligence suggests that desire for continued dissent among the citizens is low. However active cooperation also appears low, as such marital law has been continued as a precaution. Unjustified troop transgressions against the local population have been kept to an acceptable minimum.

Notable dissidents who failed to flee are currently being interrogated and will be dispatched elsewhere for enhanced interrogation. Humanitarian efforts are ongoing in the city. Citizens will be required to register in order to ease apprehension of suspected secessionists or political radicals.

Armored vehicles requested to improve ability to patrol safely as terrorists seem to have a limited supply of heavy weapons.Patrol boats required to reconnaissance coast as remaining groups are suspected to be established in remote areas.

General Francisco de Rivera, Head of Military Security District Galicia.

options.text: History is a a web of anticlimax.

iberiawars_cityfall.55.title: Liberation of Leira
iberiawars_cityfall.55.description:
For the eyes of the King: Notification regarding the successful liberation of Leira.

Sire,

It is my pleasure to inform you that the liberation of Leira has been successfully concluded, with all metropolitan areas secured in addition to the surrounding area. The likelihood of counter-attack at present seems minor. I have received a comprehensive report from the local commander, and summarize as thus:

As you are aware, our current strategy indicates that we wish to use this city as a hub for future efforts to rescue the areas controlled by the Republicans. To that end, care has been taken to limit damage to a practical military necessity. While some areas suffered moderate to high damage, most of these were residential areas away from major logistical infrastructure.

Further, moderation is being encouraged in the troops regarding their treatment of the citizens in order to ease integration and stability efforts. We are aware that public expressions of dissent are still occurring, however few instances have developed into any more than grumbling. As such, some of the more liberal within your administration can assure themselves. We are developing a range of plans to deal with dissident views which may be harmful to the Kingdom once the situation is further consolidated for you to view at a later date.

Many of our troops call Leira the gateway to the Republic. I share their hope that this war will soon end.

God Save the King

Defence Minister Fernando dos Santos Costa

options.text: The Crown recognises restraint in its benefit.

iberiawars_cityfall.56.title: Leira's Symbols
iberiawars_cityfall.56.description:
"You there, man in the coat! Turn around."

He turned, a trim and lean man wearing an ill fitting overcoat, dark brown with discolored patches. His clothing underneath was at odds with the once expensive coat, a stained green shirt with beige trousers, ripped and blackened with soot and dirt.

Behind him were two officers, neatly presented - at odds with the fatigued population keeping distance from them. "Your coat, give it to us." said one of them.

The lean man gave it to them without question, quickly taking it off. The officers examined it, taking interest in a lapel pin on its breast.

"Where did you get this?"

"My home was destroyed in the battle sirs, I've been living rough since then. The nights can get cold, so I found this coa-"

They closed the gap between them, positioning the lean man between them. He looked at them both, their brown eyes red with hostility. " This pin, it's a Republican pin." they told him, pointing to the pin they'd taken interest in.

The lean man looked at it blankly. He hadn't noticed it before."It is?"

The answer came from the pin, an officer jamming the pin into the lean man's arm. He cried out, as a fist knocked him to the ground. The Officers threw the coat in the street, and started beating the lean man. He impotently shielded himself from their boots; the city just walked past.

The coat lay in the gutter, trampled and soiled.

options.text: A young girl picked it up days later.

iberiawars_cityfall.57.title: Liberation of Lisbon
iberiawars_cityfall.57.description:
For the eyes of the King: Notification regarding the successful liberation of Lisbon.

Sire, the taking of Lisbon represents a major step forward in our efforts to restore stability to Portugal and I am deeply happy to be able to report to you that our recent campaign to secure it has been a success. Our flag now flys over the city, and I have received the reports from the local commanders describing their efforts to secure the city.

Both regular and irregular forces attempted to close the peninsula and force us into a prolonged engagement, perhaps wishing for us to exhaust ourselves in preparation for a breakout. As such lines of entrenchment and fortifications had been built. Fortunately, through the gallantry of certain officers - whose names have been forwarded to you for recognition of their merit - our soldiers were able to break through Republican lines and enter the city. Due to the rapid advance most regular units of the Republican army were encircled and destroyed in the outskirts.

Despite this success, irregular resistance remained high in the city resulting in a longer campaign than hoped, and even now we still suffer terrorist attacks from armed republicans. The wider population retains some hostility to our administration; as such we have had to repeatedly employ a firm response to local provocations. Fortunately however organized resistance has melted, and security forces assure me the current insecurity will soon cease. Individuals willing to serve their King and possessing useful skills are being screened to establish a new city administration. Further information on that shall be provided as and when it is available.

God Save the King

Defence Minister Fernando dos Santos Costa

options.text: Despite their reluctance, light shall shine on our golden city.

iberiawars_cityfall.58.title: Liberation of Lisbon
iberiawars_cityfall.58.description:
"At least the city looks as miserable as we are," Francisco thought to himself as he and his captured comrades marched, heads bowed and packed like cattle, through the ruins of the once beautiful city of Lisbon.

Enough of the roads were cleared of rubble for the victory parade to proceed without issue, but overwhelmingly the inner city was still little more than ruins and debris, hardly resembling a place suitable for human life. From the once proud buildings to the lush parks, punctuating lunar craters and jagged wrecks declared their mockery of what had once been beautiful.

But such matters were hardly his concern anymore. He and his fellow prisoners marched through the shattered streets before the hollowed eyes of the populace until they would reach their destination and swear loyalty to the so-called King.

Francisco noticed in his quick glances that within those empty eyes of the crowd, the mood seemed to be in sync with his own. He glimpsed measured hatred in the eyes of a bold few as they watched this sham play out, standing out in the disheveled mass. Their hatred never reached their mouths or hands however as proud soldiers stood all around. Above them, brief and occasional flashes informed all of watching snipers, sentinels ensuring the sheep didn't stray away.Francisco continued on with his brothers, his shame matched only by his despondency. The heart of Portugal had been taken and soon, he would pledge himself to the idol of those who had taken it.

options.text: He wasn't sure what the oaths of broken men were worth.

iberiawars_cityfall.59.title: Liberation of Lisbon
iberiawars_cityfall.59.description:
Luis hobbled along the rubble-strewn streets of Lisbon, his makeshift wooden crutch occasionally catching on a crack in the ground or some stray brick. The ghost of his leg ached in the humid morning air, and he silently cursed his condition.

He had been a soldier for the Republic. All he had to show for it was a missing leg and red flags hanging over the city he had been fighting to protect. With sore arms, he collapsed onto a mostly intact bench to regain his strength. Across the street, he saw the local butcher sweeping broken glass in front of his shop. A woman he couldn't quite remember the name of was walking by and as she passed the butcher Luis heard an all too familiar phrase. "Long Live the Revolution!" she said, the butcher responding in kind.

Throughout the rest of Luis's day as he attempted to sort out some errands, dragging himself through a city slowly trying to recover some semblance of normality, he heard it over and over again. "Long Live the Revolution!", "Long Live the Revolution!" over and over again like a religious creed said during a mass. In greetings and farewells, it seemed the revolution was ever present.

The individual words in the phrase had stopped sounding like words to Luis's ears amidst the cacophony of identical greetings, even making him wince every time he heard it. Ever since his city had been lost, it was as if the citizens had been replaced by socialist caricatures of themselves. Even Luis, always something of a cynic, hadn't expected even the most innocuous portions of everyday speech to become a political action. How fast those he'd been sworn to defend had suddenly become revolutionaries.

options.text: He would have laughed at the absurdity, but the phantom pain was ever present.

iberiawars_cityfall.60.title: Liberation of Madrid
iberiawars_cityfall.60.description:
Communique to the Office of the President of the Spanish Republic,

Sir,

We have successfully secured the city of Madrid. Troops and material are moving into the city. The final bastions of organized resistance have either capitulated or been neutralized.

The city was captured in a surprisingly sound condition. Resistance was fierce but that was within our expectations as we organized the assault. Numerous hostile units throughout the city used conventional and guerilla tactics to prevent our advance, fortunately most of the widespread damage has been limited to the outskirts.

We have evidence of mass intimidation and conscription of residents in an attempt to utilize them against our advance. Captured administrators and officers suspected to be involved are being relocated for further interrogation on their methods and crimes. There is a large number of irregular captives being held on the outskirts of the city awaiting the decision of the government in regards to their fate.

We discovered some local uprisings within the city that weakened enemy strongholds, with the unfortunate loss of many documents as the public took to looting and burning. Rather than criticize, a timeline has been created of the essential truth and shall be distributed by agents in cities that remain occupied in the hopes of spurring more unrest.

The Media have already submitted applications for morale boosting broadcasts and events to be filmed and aired around the city, which shall be passed to the relevant officials in due course.

In regards to civilian casualties, they were within acceptable ranges.

options.text: A bloodied jewel of a new crown.

iberiawars_cityfall.61.title: Liberation of Malaga
iberiawars_cityfall.61.description:
TOP SECRET

COMMUNIQUE TO THE WAR MINISTER: FOR IMMEDIATE ATTENTION

Sir,

The security situation within Malaga remains unstable despite the cessation of organized resistance within the city limits and its transfer to security forces.

THe fighting for the city was characterized by a high proportion of irregular resistance to our forces, with paramilitary confrontations at the City Hall, the regional university hospital and La Rosaleda Stadium to name three notable locations of sieges. Damage to public buildings and areas rebels identified as defensible has been considerable. With attacks from terrorists continuing proper reconstruction, as well as the consistent flow of supplies into the city, carry prohibitive risks. Morale among the ranks of security personnel has collapsed due to the heavy and consistent threat of terrorist assault, further exacerbating the difficult relationship between the population and the MSD.

More Intelligence assets and personnel are desperately required, as well as armored vehicles to make traversal through the most dangerous parts of the city less risky.Materials to begin construction of Supervised Refugee Centers outside city limits in order to disperse the populations of the more unstable districts also requested.

General Luis Delgado, Head of Military Security District South

options.text: Cowards think not wearing uniforms will hide them. We will see them.

iberiawars_cityfall.62.title: Liberation of Oviedo
iberiawars_cityfall.62.description:
Communique to the Office of the President of the Spanish Republic,

Sir,

Oviedo has been secured, with positions being entrenched on the perimeter. However, it seems unlikely that any successful attack will be able to force us out in the immediate future. Attacks on local logistics remain, however military supplies remain sufficient. There is a developing humanitarian crisis developing however amongst the civilian population.

Oviedo saw considerable hostilities, with the city's defenses having been designed with a long siege in mind. Literature recovered from the city demonstrates this was a central propaganda tool by the defending garrison in the employment of civilian aid. As such, during our assaults we faced well entrenched positions with contact points often in close proximity to non-combatants.

The extent to which civilians were forced to remain in the city or chose to stay is as yet unclear with rivaling testimonies. Further, the exact purpose of them is also unclear as intelligence suggests they were predominantly laborers or paramilitaries, but the high number of women and children and their frequent proximities to assaults suggest a more nefarious human shield possibility. Analysis and interrogations are ongoing.

Regrettably, that does mean that there was a very high number of collateral deaths despite our best efforts. The approximate numbers have been suppressed, although the Media have been provided with a more palatable lower end prediction. Most of these have been blamed on atrocities committed by the defenders. Some of the large capacity grave sites have been photographed and labeled as constructed by nationalist troops in order to avoid an unnecessary effect on public morale.

options.text: We gave them the propaganda number.

iberiawars_cityfall.63.title: Liberation of Pamplona
iberiawars_cityfall.63.description:
TOP SECRET

COMMUNIQUE TO THE WAR MINISTER: FOR IMMEDIATE ATTENTION

Sir

Limited resources. Difficult terrain. Excess of dissidents suspected locally.

Organised resistance destroyed. Shock attacks routed forces. Hostile units suspected to have fled and reorganised.Terrorist activity significant. Improvised explosives, ambushes and assassinations frequently employed against security personnel.

Actions Taken: Dissident arrests and emergency sentencing, martial law, controlled demolitions. Hostile regions identified and quarantined.

Concerns: Overstretched units. High attritional losses. Hostile population limits operational effectiveness outside core areas of the city.

Request: Reinforcement. Updated rules of engagement for the region. Materials for construction of 3 more detainment camps. Details shall follow in report.

General Emilio Huesca, Head of Military Security District Basque-Navarre.

options.text: From behind every wall, car or hill comes a bullet.

iberiawars_cityfall.64.title: Liberation of Porto
iberiawars_cityfall.64.description:
Belmiro and Hélio watched as their men squatted in front of the Porto City Hall's arches. After all the charges were in a position, they'd retreated to a safe distance to watch their handiwork. Black explosives now clung to the bricks like ticks, wires flowing inside, but there would be no slow atrophy. With a single click of the detonator, the arches crumbled inward with the hall's clock tower imploding in on itself. The decorative pool rippled before becoming soiled with a thick layer of dust, turning the greenish water grey.

"Seems wasteful, doesn't it?" Belmiro muttered as his eyes flicked between the ruins and the celebrating soldiers. "You know someone is going to have to rebuild another hall, right? With our luck,after the war is over, they'll probably put us to work on it." Leaning on the railing, he shook his head. "Why was the order even given?"

"Can't change the world without smashing a few monuments," Hélio reasoned something that sounded vaguely like theory. Without a concrete explanation from the high command, that was as good as anything. "Once, the castles of the old kings seemed eternal."

Belmiro snorted. "But their castles are still around. Some of them are even — you know — used."

Hélio waved his hand dismissively toward the settling dust. "By getting rid of the old, you are making space for the new." Turning to his squadmate, he slapped his back, making Belmiro straighten up. "And if it all goes wrong, we'll just tear down whatever they build next. We — the people — are in charge now."

Belmiro didn't respond right away. Instead, he stared at the rubble.

options.text: Maybe.

iberiawars_cityfall.65.title: Liberation of Setubal
iberiawars_cityfall.65.description:
For the eyes of the King: Notification regarding the successful liberation of Setubal.

Sire, Setubal now lies securely in our control. It is my pleasure to inform you that your armed forces conducted themselves admirably in the conduct of the assault, to such an extent that our propaganda efforts shall make special mention of the success of this assault.

The securing of the city was achieved with far less need for destruction than had initially been feared. Fighting was intense in the surrounding areas of the city, however through the skill of our officers our forces could rout much of the enemy and force them to retire away from Setubal itself. As such, our forces within the city faced a much diminished force. Our momentum carried the day with a large amount of prisoners and captured material taken. A series of Holding Camps have been constructed near the city for prisoners pending transportation to more secure sites.

As such many of Setubal's historic monuments and buildings have remained intact, if not undamaged. This is obviously an astounding victory for Portugal herself and images of soldiers visiting some of the most notable buildings will be distributed to newspapers soon.
