Due to our success in taking prisoners, intelligence on established terrorist cells could be extracted swiftly and efficiently and a combination of rapid arrests and displays of force have resulted in a city far more peaceful than had been prepared for. Civilian losses were well within acceptable ranges. Also, the majority of the City's administration was unable to flee as a result of our rapid assault. They have been detained and are currently being interviewed. Discussion on what we shall do with these administrators shall be discussed at our next meeting.

God Save The King

Defence Minister Fernando dos Santos Costa

options.text: With God on our side, our forces are carried on the wind.

iberiawars_cityfall.66.title: Liberation of Setubal
iberiawars_cityfall.66.description:
To say they were herded into this place like pigs would be inaccurate; a farmer would have at least cared enough about his animals to ensure their value. Their captors had no such concerns, something abundantly clear as they shoved them through the narrow corridors of the stadium, bumping and crashing into one another in a desperate stampede to the relative freedom of the clearing.

Afonso was lucky to have made it out without being stomped or kicked to death and he savored the fresh air like it was wine, many of those who had been with him were hardly as lucky.

Then came the wait.

They stood there in the middle of the stadium as more and more of their comrades were shoveled in like rats. Before long they all began talking, an attempt to make their miserable situation slightly more bearable through a veil of civility, like a losing team trying to move past humiliation.

"I came here a lot before, this is the Estadio do Bonfim" said Gonzalo. Alfonso didn't know him well but unlike him was a native to the area along with many of the other captives. "My brothers and I would come here often to watch the games."

"Surprised it looks so pristine, from here it looks as if there was hardly any war at all" another prisoner noted of the turf before the voice of barked angry orders silenced them all. They looked up to the stands to see men setting up machine guns across the stadium, positioned such that the entire field could be covered.

Suddenly all their attempts at conversation evaporated.

options.text: Game. Set. Match.

iberiawars_cityfall.67.title: Liberation of Setubal
iberiawars_cityfall.67.description:
Heinrich awoke as the door cracked in two, the battering ram breaking the thin wood nearly in twain, before being kicked down. His room was little more than a closet with a bed, and he sat up in shock and fear. Armed men stood watching him in civilian clothes, no uniforms besides a red rag tied around their arms. Questions died in his throat; despite his pajamas he felt naked.

Keeping their weapons visible the armed men parted, allowing a single policeman to enter. The only uniformed intruder, he carried himself with authority, completely at ease with the men around him. "Senyor, comtchamas?" he asked, calmly but firmly. Heinrich tried to get out of bed but the Officer raised his hand, an nonverbal command to stop, before repeating his question. It was a question that Heinrich couldn't understand, his slim Portuguese little help against the thick accent of the Officer.

"Uh, deshculpa... no compriendo... pilot du linha-"

The officer rolled his eyes. "Twu Esh lmao reshistrado nesht epartmento?" he asked, annoyance seeping into his voice while drawing a swastika in the air with his fingers. Heinrich nervously looked back at the armed men then to the officer. The Officer had said something like "lmao" while signing a swastika...Alemao? He was asking if he was German?

"Ja, uh, sim. Ich denke schon?"

The officer nodded and turned around, leaving Heinrich still frozen on his bed. "Matu" he said to the men.

Heinrich had only moments to guess the meaning of the command before the men opened fire, Heinrich's ears briefly filled with furious clattering - he didn't have time to scream as bullets destroyed him.

options.text: The bloodied corpse was left where it was, a swastika crudely painted beside the door frame.

iberiawars_cityfall.68.title: Liberation of Sevilla
iberiawars_cityfall.68.description:
TOP SECRET

COMMUNIQUE TO THE WAR MINISTER: FOR IMMEDIATE ATTENTION

Sir,

The situation in Sevilla refuses to stabilize despite our successful capture of the city which lay at the heart of the Republican rebellion. Rebel groups from multiple factions continue to fight our security forces as well as each other. Street violence within Seville is not yet consistently suppressed.

Lethal force has been authorized dependent on officer initiative. Some officers have levied complaints regarding the excessive conduct of Falngist aligned troops, however given the difficult situation it has been decided to rather deploy Falangist units to the most troublesome areas rather than restrain them.

Supplies are currently being lost at an average rate of 40% per shipment thanks to mines, partisan ambush and raiding. Starvation is further undermining the security situation with raids on supply depots. Attempts to create secure refugee camps outside the city continue but the local population in high risk areas remain resistant to relocation. Harsher methods may have to be taken.

General Luis Delgado, Head of Military Security District South

options.text: If they bite the hand that feeds, we have no choice but to punish.

iberiawars_cityfall.69.title: Liberation of Valencia
iberiawars_cityfall.69.description:
TOP SECRET

COMMUNIQUE TO THE WAR MINISTER: FOR IMMEDIATE ATTENTION

Sir,

Valencia's capture and subsequent placement under military administration has been achieved with relative success, most notably in the strategic objectives regarding the limitation of rebel access to the Mediterranean - to which the loss of a major part is undoubtedly an achievement for our cause.

Regrettably there have been complications in the cessation of active terrorist activity within the Military Zone after the establishment of martial law. With the city being secured with less destruction than was originally projected, most combat being outside of the city, it was thought that the area would be easier to stabilize. Instead large amounts of logistical sabotage in the port, city and surrounding region as well as persistent terrorist raids on convoys has created a frustrating situation where supplies from abroad hoped to enter via Valencia cannot while supplies and reinforcements from elsewhere in Spain struggle to distribute in the area.

In order to make Valencia a secure lynchpin of controlling the Spanish coast and Mediterranean access we urgently require at least 2000 men plus equipment and support for use in garrisoning duty, as well as delivery of 48 requested armored vehicles and 32 Commercial Vehicle Weapon Carriers for expansion and reinforcement of the armored cavalry assigned to convoy guarding.

General Carlos Costa, Head of Military Security District East.

options.text: We must have what we require to ease the rot.

iberiawars_cityfall.70.title: Liberation of Valladolid
iberiawars_cityfall.70.description:
Communique to the Office of the President of the Spanish Republic,

Sir,

Valladolid has been secured, marking a major landmark in our Northern Campaign. The city was maybe one of the most fortified cities thus far in the campaign, with our assessment being that securing the city will be a major part in guaranteeing victory in the War.

The city had become a maze of entrenched positions, ambush traps and fortified buildings. Further, the city remains home to one of the most ideologically opposed civilian populations we have reclaimed so far.

The city is a hub of monarchist sentiments leading to a large amount of paramilitary resistance in addition to the troops positioned. Heavy losses as such were incurred, requiring the usage of heavy weapons and indirect fire tactics. The result has been a large degree of damage across the city with large displacements of civilians. Food and water deprivation amongst refugees is critical, with current strategies failing to aid most.

The retreat was sudden and unexpected, apparently without prior organization suggesting either a breakdown of communications or a sudden change of strategy. Whatever the cause, the ability of enemy forces to withdraw was hindered by the large number of refugees. Some forced their way through the bands while others were slowed enough to be neutralized.

Due to the large degree of radicalization within the city, as well as the degree of damage, many areas are being relocated to humanitarian camps in the surrounding area. The Media are being barred from much of the interior of the city citing security concerns as we continue to sweep for hostile units.

options.text: Rather free dust than enslaved opulence.

iberiawars_cityfall.71.title: Liberation of Vigo
iberiawars_cityfall.71.description:
TOP SECRET

COMMUNIQUE TO THE WAR MINISTER: FOR IMMEDIATE ATTENTION

Sir

Vigo is now completely under the administration of the Military Security District. Regrettably Vigo saw a higher than expected degree of irregular resistance and as such sustained a litany of losses. The industrial capacity of the city has been much affected, with the industrial areas seeing the brunt of resistance. Further, reports of troops looting have been reported, which regrettably have led to tensions between the security forces and the populace. Intelligence suggests that while not critical, Vigo will require attention for some time to be pacified.

Terrorism continues, at first minimal but local stories of criminality committed by our forces have led to some increase. Efforts to combat disinformation are ongoing. The economic assessments made prior to the assault, when intelligence suggested a relatively low intensity assault, must be reassessed. Interrogations of dissidents are ongoing, with notable individuals due to be relocated to specialized facilities.

A team must be sent to reassess Galicia's industrial abilities, as well as resources to establish a local media campaign to soften our image in order to prevent sympathies for dissidents causing expensive problems in the future.

options.text: Vigo shall cheer, for Spanish peace and prosperity has returned: we command it.

iberiawars_cityfall.72.title: Liberation of Zaragoza
iberiawars_cityfall.72.description:
Communique to the Office of the President of the Spanish Republic,

Sir,

Zaragoza has fallen, with our advance units confirming the total retreat of hostile forces.

Zaragoza has suffered substantial damage. Their units appeared to have high morale and good fortifications, with the city having been prepared to withstand a protracted conflict. This was within expectations, due to Zaragoza's symbolic value to all factions of the former regime as one of the first cities to fall in the previous Civil War.

The worst of the fighting fell in the city's historic districts, a gambit that we would not utilize substantial heavy weaponry in those areas. Limited use was permitted and maintained a mobile frontline, to the expense of the city. Losses to ambushes and guerilla tactics remained high throughout the city, increasing as the defense began to disintegrate.

All areas of the city have experienced at least some damage and there is a high risk of remaining Nationalist radicals or guerilla forces. Civilian opinion is split; while the Republic enjoys some support there is a majority in the city who are at least sympathetic to the old regime. Possible educational initiatives are being trialed to reeducate the hostile population. The collapse of local civilian logistics has aggravated this.

Regrettably, there have been instances of troop reprisals against surrendered soldiers and local administrators. Such instances were without formal approval and any information related to the incidents is being controlled for fear of sparking civil unrest. Involved units will be redeployed, however in the interest of limiting any possible leak of information no formal disciplinary action shall be taken.

options.text: All for the greater good.

iberiawars_cityfall.73.title: Liberation of Leiria
iberiawars_cityfall.73.description:
Artur looked up at the sky, a dim glow being the only indication that the sun existed beyond the smoke and ash. Still, it was more pleasant than staring at the husks all around him. The grey ruins looked barely enough like buildings to notice the lost and unappreciated qualities of life, like staring into the face of a mangled corpse.

The sound of his comrades’ boots set the tempo for their march: a crunch of concrete followed by the crackling of glass — like brittle ice breaking apart. Being a border city put it squarely between the barrages from both North and South, it was no wonder that Leira ended up like this.

He had visited the city once as a kid, being utterly overwhelmed by the cacophony of cars and people. Now, Leira was still, as if struggling to breathe. There were no chirps of birds or sloshing of the fountains. There were no children running through the streets and no yells from parents. There was nothing. There was no one — not a soul, save for his sunken-eyed comrades.

His sergeant turned to confirm that the rest of his men were still with him and that he hadn’t wandered into hell by accident. He opened his mouth, searching for words, but no sound came out. Instead, he turned back and trudged forward. However, Artur had glimpsed the uncertainty in his eyes. After all, there were no landmarks to mark their way — no goal to march towards.

options.text: Could this still be called a city?

iberiawars_OFN_POR.1.title: Azores and Madeira
iberiawars_OFN_POR.1.description:
FROM: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
TO: The Council of Ministers
SUBJECT: Negotiating the return of the Azores and Madeira

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has received a request from the American Department of State to negotiate the potential return of the illegally occupied archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands").

- The islands are under the control of the illegitimate Portuguese Confederation after their failure to seize control of Portugal during our last war. This occupation is a violation of our sovereignty by an insurrectionist movement.
- The islands are a vital component of our power projection in the Atlantic. It is imperative that we return these islands to our control as soon as possible.
- The Portuguese Confederation is a pro-OFN organization, with lobbies in OFN member states such as Brazil. Should the Confederation ever take power, it will turn Portugal into an important foothold for the OFN in Europe.
- While the OFN may prefer the Confederation, they are aware of the limited power of the Confederation in its current state. At the time of writing, the OFN has not engaged in direct and formal talks with the Confederation.
- The OFN will require concessions from Lisbon in order to support recognizing our claims over the islands. Topics may include OFN access to Lajes' airfields, investment rights in Portugal, and military aid.
- Should we fail to negotiate with the OFN, they may prefer to deal with the Confederation outright. From the islands, the Confederation may be able to launch an invasion of Portugal if sufficiently trained and equipped.

We recommend engagement with the Americans on this issue.

options.text: Agreed. Let's see where this gets us.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.2.title: Azores and Madeira
iberiawars_OFN_POR.2.description:
FROM: US State Department
TO: President [USA.GetLeader]
SUBJECT: Negotiating the return of the Azores and Madeira

After further consideration of the Portugal issue, we have opened a channel to Lisbon. They are interested in negotiating the return of the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands").

- Following the defeat of pro-Republican forces in the Portuguese Civil War, remnants of the National Portuguese Liberation Front retreated to the islands. They have since been in exile as the Portuguese Confederation, refusing Lisbon's authority.
- Located in the Atlantic Ocean, the islands are a key component of Portugal's power projection in the Atlantic.
- The Portuguese Confederation is a pro-OFN organization, and Lisbon fears that we may prefer what they see as an insurrectionary movement over recognizing the current government. This may make them amenable to negotiation.
- While the Confederation has petitioned for OFN support, we have requested that they politely ignore them for the moment. At present, they are exiles with limited training and support. If we want to recognize Lisbon over them, we cannot have the OFN approaching them openly and early.
- If we are to recognize Lisbon's claim over the islands, we will require concessions. Topics may include OFN access to Lajes Airfield, investment rights in Portugal, and military aid.
- Should negotiations fail, we will be free to engage with the Portuguese Confederation. Options may include backing the Confederation's landing on Portugal's shores.

A full State Department briefing will be organized in the coming days.

options.text: Lisbon's lovely this time of year, isn't it?"

iberiawars_OFN_POR.3.title: Azores and Madeira, I: Lajes Airfield
iberiawars_OFN_POR.3.description:
FROM: US State Department
TO: President [USA.GetLeader]
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, I: Lajes Airfield

We have commenced negotiations with the Portuguese government in Lisbon regarding the potential return of the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). Our first topic of contention is Lajes Airfield.

- Located on Ilha Terceira in the Azores, the Lajes Airfield is the largest of its kind on the islands. Located less than a thousand miles off the coast of Portugal, its strategic value is immense for our ability to operate in the Atlantic.
- As such, we require a status of forces agreement ("SOFA") that will allow American soldiers to be stationed in the base and also permits American airplanes to utilize the airfield.
- Lisbon, already skeptical of our intentions, will undoubtedly see this as an attack on their own sovereignty. Whether they accept it as a cost of doing business with the United States is another matter.

- Ideally, we want a guaranteed SOFA that will grant us full and permanent access to the airfield, without the potential for renegotiation by the Portuguese government. We expect that Lisbon will likely expect this to be our opening.
- In order to assuage their concerns and set a better tone for further talks, we may instead opt to propose a temporary agreement, pending renegotiation at a future date. Lisbon will better appreciate this acknowledgement of their sovereignty.

We await further instructions.

options.text: Let's not be hasty here. A temporary agreement will do.
We want a proper SOFA. Lisbon just has to live with it.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.4.title: Azores and Madeira, I: Lajes Airfield
iberiawars_OFN_POR.4.description:
FROM: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
TO: The Council of Ministers
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, I: Lajes Airfield

We have received the first demand from the Americans regarding the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). They have demanded a full status of forces agreement ("SOFA") concerning Lajes Airfield.

- Located on Ilha Terceira, Lajes Airfield is the largest of its kind on the islands. It is a fundamental component of our military capacity in the Atlantic Ocean.
- Desiring extended capacity in the Atlantic Ocean, they wish to have an American military presence in Lajes Airfield.
- The SOFA would permit US forces to be stationed in reserved areas of Lajes Airfield, including soldiers, vehicles, and support staff.
- This SOFA would be binding and indefinite, ensuring that the US military will become a permanent presence in the eastern Atlantic.
- This was expected; the airfield itself is already effectively under the OFN's control, and they wish to maintain that even if the islands are returned to our control.

- An American presence in Lajes may prove to be controversial to our European neighbors. Further, it would be a perceptible blow to our sovereignty if we allowed foreign troops to be stationed in such a strategically important base. We remind the Council of Ministers that they have the authority and the freedom to defend our military sovereignty.
- However, we currently do not control the islands. They remain illegally occupied with the implicit acceptance of the OFN. If we are to secure the islands, negotiating with the occupation's backers is necessary to avoid a military entanglement we cannot win.

options.text: We can't hold back negotiations over this. Accept it.
Lajes is on our island, not theirs. Reject this.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.5.title: Azores and Madeira, I: Lajes Airfield
iberiawars_OFN_POR.5.description:
FROM: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
TO: The Council of Ministers
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, I: Lajes Airfield

We have received the first demand from the Americans concerning the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). They have requested a limited status of forces agreement ("SOFA") between the United States and Portugal in Lajes Airfield.

- Located on Ilha Terceira, Lajes Airfield is the largest of its kind on the islands. It is a fundamental component of our military capacity in the Atlantic Ocean.
- Desiring extended capacity in the Atlantic Ocean, they wish to have an American military presence in Lajes Airfield.
- The SOFA would permit US forces to be stationed in reserved areas of Lajes Airfield, including soldiers, vehicles, and support staff.
- The Americans have offered a temporary SOFA that can be renegotiated five years after current negotiations end. This does open up the potential for future dialogue.
- The Ministry of Foreign Affairs expected the US, who have de facto control over Lajes during this illegal occupation, to demand full control. A temporary agreement suggests a conciliatory tone.

- An American presence in Lajes may prove to be controversial to our European neighbors. Further, it would be a perceptible blow to our sovereignty if we allowed foreign troops to be stationed in such a strategically important base. We remind the Council of Ministers that they have the authority and the freedom to defend our military sovereignty.
- However, the Americans have offered terms more reasonable than we expected. A temporary agreement opens up the hope for a full restoration of sovereignty in the future.

options.text: Temporary or not, Lajes is our airfield. Reject this.
This is more reasonable than we expected. Accept this.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.6.title: Azores and Madeira, I: Lajes Airfield
iberiawars_OFN_POR.6.description:
FROM: US State Department
TO: President [USA.GetLeader]
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, I: Lajes Airfield

We are continuing negotiations with the Portuguese government in Lisbon regarding the potential return of the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). We are still engaged in discussion regarding a status of forces agreement ("SOFA") for Lajes Airfield.

- We previously demanded a full SOFA that would allow for American troops to be stationed permanently in Lajes Airfield.
- The Portuguese Ministry of Foreign Affairs has rejected this proposal, claiming that such a demand would be a violation of their military sovereignty. During our delegation's talks, they also suggested that we were effectively forcing this agreement onto them.
- The Portuguese consider the islands to already be under an illegal occupation. American troops stationed in Lajes Airfield on a permanent basis may suggest to them that the occupation was never removed, but downscaled.

- We may consider easing our current proposal to a temporary SOFA that would allow for American troops to be stationed until five years after current negotiations end, at which time the SOFA would be renegotiated.
- Lisbon's concern about American troops on the islands is already an early obstacle, one perhaps too great to overcome at this time. If we shelve the topic now and prove ourselves a reliable partner, we may be able to revisit this topic at a later time.
- Alternatively, we may consider withdrawing from the talks entirely. Lajes Airfield is critical to our ability to project power into the Mediterranean. If Lisbon refuses to engage further on this subject, we may still be able to acquire the airfield by other means.

options.text: Maybe we can accept something less permanent. Go with the alternative.
Let's just put this aside for the moment.
To hell with this; let's take our chances with the Confederation. Leave the talks.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.7.title: Azores and Madeira, I: Lajes Airfield
iberiawars_OFN_POR.7.description:
FROM: US State Department
TO: President [USA.GetLeader]
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, I: Lajes Airfield

We are continuing negotiations with the Portuguese government in Lisbon regarding the potential return of the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). We are still engaged in discussion regarding a status of forces agreement ("SOFA") for Lajes Airfield.

- We previously demanded a temporary SOFA that would allow for American ground and air forces to be stationed in Lajes Airfield until five years after current negotiations end, at which time the SOFA would be renegotiated.
- The Portuguese Ministry of Foreign Affairs has rejected this proposal, claiming that such a demand would be a violation of their military sovereignty. During our delegation's talks, they also suggested that we were effectively forcing this agreement onto them.
- The Portuguese consider the islands to already be under an illegal occupation. American troops stationed in Lajes Airfield are not acceptable to them under any circumstances, whether or not the agreement is temporary.

- We may offer a further compromise to our agreement: limiting our military presence in Lajes to a reduced number of on-site troops, while maintaining both a standard air presence and support staff.
- Given the reluctance on Portugal's part to allow for an American military presence on the islands, we may wish to shelve this issue for the remainder of these negotiations. If we prove ourselves a reliable partner to Lisbon later, we may be able to revisit this topic in future talks.

options.text: Fine, let's just drop it for the moment.
Loath as we are to accept it, why not? Give them another compromise.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.8.title: Azores and Madeira, I: Lajes Airfield
iberiawars_OFN_POR.8.description:
FROM: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
TO: The Council of Ministers
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, I: Lajes Airfield

We continue to discuss the first demand from the Americans concerning the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). They have insisted on a limited status of forces agreement ("SOFA") between the United States and Portugal in Lajes Airfield.

- Located on Ilha Terceira, Lajes Airfield is the largest of its kind on the islands. It is a fundamental component of our military capacity in the Atlantic Ocean, and the Americans have requested a continuing presence in this airfield.
- The SOFA would permit US forces to be stationed in reserved areas of Lajes Airfield, including soldiers, vehicles, and support staff.
- The American delegation has offered a temporary agreement that can be renegotiated five years after current negotiations end.
- We previously rejected this proposal, as we have continuing concerns over the presence of American troops on sovereign Portuguese territory, particularly territory of significant strategic value.
- While the Americans insist on a military presence, they have offered to severely limit the amount of ground forces that can be stationed at Lajes, while retaining the previously-proposed amount of air forces.

- Though we reaffirm our concerns over American troops in Lajes, this is perhaps the best possible outcome on this topic that we can receive.
- The Americans are insistent on a military presence and will not budge on this issue. If we cannot come to an agreement here, we will not be able to proceed with the rest of the discussion regarding the islands.

options.text: If the Americans want to blow up talks over this, fine. Withdraw our diplomats.
I suppose that's a better compromise. Accept it.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.9.title: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment
iberiawars_OFN_POR.9.description:
FROM: US State Department
TO: President [USA.GetLeader]
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment

We are continuing negotiations with the Portuguese government in Lisbon regarding the potential return of the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). We are opening up a new topic for discussion: access to Portuguese markets for American investors.

- Portugal's economy has experienced sizable growth since the end of the Second World War. Economic investment at this time was limited to internal investors within the Iberian Union and secondary investors in Europe.
- A significant portion of its industry was destroyed during the Portuguese Civil War. It is Lisbon's priority to repair the industrial damage inflicted by this conflict. American investments may be crucial to the redevelopment of Portuguese industry.
- By securing investment rights, America will receive an entry into European markets, which have remained closed to us since the end of the Second World War.
- We can offer Lisbon a reconstruction plan involving substantial investment by the American government. This will require a significant amount of capital on our part, and Lisbon may regard this as an attempt at economic dominance; however, it would be our most generous offer.
- We may also offer a limited plan attached to private investment rights, in exchange for preferential treatment towards American businesses. While Lisbon may be more hostile towards the private sector, private funds may secure more than our plan.
- Alternatively, we can offer a far more limited plan, ensuring that American economic activity remains within levels defined by Lisbon. While economically less impactful than our other options, Lisbon may appreciate our restraint.

options.text: They need what we can give them. Let's fund it ourselves.
We can't go bankrupt bailing out Portugal. Let's get the private sector in.
Lisbon has to think we're doing them a favor. Let's send them the limited plan.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.10.title: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment
iberiawars_OFN_POR.10.description:
FROM: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
TO: The Council of Ministers
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment

We have received the second demand from the Americans concerning the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). They have requested an agreement concerning American foreign investment in Portugal.

- Among the damage sustained in the civil war, our industrial capacity suffered due to bombings, raids, and other acts of sabotage by our enemy. Our economy continues to shrink even as we attempt to rebuild.
- The United States has offered a large and detailed reconstruction plan, in which the US government will extensively invest in our economy to stimulate and accelerate economic growth.
- While American private capital may contribute via bonds and other financial instruments, the administration of these funds will be the US State Department.
- We estimate significant economic growth over the next three years as a result of this plan; however, the Ministry remains concerned about the potential for inequitable and perhaps exploitative economic bonds placed upon us by Washington through this plan.

- We can choose to accept this plan as-is. The amount of investments they propose may be what our economy needs in order to rebuild after the Civil War.
- We may also reject this plan outright, stating to Washington that we will not agree to any terms with risks violating our economic sovereignty.
- Alternatively, we may wish to negotiate a compromise. We can reject the recovery plan in its current form, but remain open to economic aid.

options.text: We need that capital, no matter what. Agree to the plan.
Only Portugal should manage Portugal's economy. Reject the plan.
See if we can negotiate more limited aid rather than a full plan.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.11.title: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment
iberiawars_OFN_POR.11.description:
FROM: US State Department
TO: President [USA.GetLeader]
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment

We are continuing negotiations with the Portuguese government in Lisbon regarding the potential return of the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). We are continuing discussion regarding access to Portuguese markets for American investors.

- We previously proposed an economic recovery plan, which would have involved immense investment into Portuguese industrial projects to rebuild destroyed infrastructure and industrial facilities.
- The Portuguese government has rejected this plan, claiming that they do not wish to discuss any outsized American influence over their economy.
- This is a flat dismissal of the topic; we will not even be able to negotiate industrial aid as a compromise position.

- In light of this, we may withdraw from the talks outright. If Lisbon is unwilling to negotiate on the economy at all, even as they struggle to recover from the damage inflicted by the Portuguese Civil War, it may not bode well for future topics.
- Alternatively, if we do not wish to walk away from the negotiations, we can move on to our final topic.

options.text: No, we still need to come to a conclusion here. Let's keep talking.
If they don't want to talk, fine. Let's walk away.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.12.title: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment
iberiawars_OFN_POR.12.description:
FROM: US State Department
TO: President [USA.GetLeader]
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment

We are continuing negotiations with the Portuguese government in Lisbon regarding the potential return of the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). We are continuing discussion regarding access to Portuguese markets for American investors.

- We previously proposed an economic recovery plan, which would have involved immense investment into Portuguese industrial projects to rebuild destroyed infrastructure and industrial facilities.
- The Portuguese government has rejected this plan, claiming that they do not wish to discuss any outsized American influence over their economy.
- However, they are willing to discuss an economic aid package, one which will not involve direct and immense American investment, but will assist their economic recovery efforts.

- Our recommendation is a financial aid package to assist Portuguese reconstruction. In exchange, we will request privileges and preferential assistance for private American firms and investors operating in the Portuguese market. This will allow us to maintain an economic presence in Europe.
- Alternatively, we can make clear from the outset that we will limit our private investors' activities in Portugal. Lisbon may be concerned with the kind of treatment we expect them to give to American firms. By declaring our own stringent limits, we can assure them that we do not mean to place undue restraints and boundaries on another country's markets.

options.text: Let's keep Lisbon happy. Propose the limited aid package.
We need to keep our foot in the door here. Propose the aid package and investment rights.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.13.title: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment
iberiawars_OFN_POR.13.description:
FROM: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
TO: The Council of Ministers
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment

We have received the second demand from the Americans concerning the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). They have requested an agreement concerning American foreign investment in Portugal.

- The United States has proposed a large economic aid package to help reconstruction efforts for Portuguese infrastructure and industry. In exchange, we will need to give investment rights to the United States, which would grant special privileges and favorable treatment to American companies and investors.
- The package itself is sizable, though the Ministry remains concerned about the rights that the United States wishes us to give their investors. A full list of demands is attached to this document.
- If we agree, we may incur the wrath of local proprietors across all sectors and firms of all sizes, who may view the generous attitude we will need to take with American companies as a risk to their own financial well-being.

- We can accept the deal as-is. Given the economic damage we have suffered in the Civil War, any amount of aid that the Americans can grant may be worth the privileges we have to extend.
- Alternatively, we can request a modification to the existing deal, limiting the amount of privileges given to American investors.
- We can also reject the deal. While we need all the help we can get in rebuilding, and we need to end the threat of the Confederation, we cannot trade away our sovereignty to the Americans.

options.text: We need the money. Agree to the terms of the aid package.
Americans are capable of reason. Ask for concessions.
They're asking for too much, and they'll always ask for too much. Reject the deal.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.14.title: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment
iberiawars_OFN_POR.14.description:
FROM: US State Department
TO: President [USA.GetLeader]
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment

We are continuing negotiations with the Portuguese government in Lisbon regarding the potential return of the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). We are continuing discussion regarding access to Portuguese markets for American investors.

- We previously proposed an economic recovery plan, which would have involved special privileges and rights to American businesses in exchange for a large economic aid package.
- The Portuguese government has rejected this plan, claiming this would threaten Portuguese sovereignty and may lead to American hegemony in their own markets.
- However, they have presented a counteroffer, one which will have fewer rights for our firms and investors, but also requests less aid from our part.

- While this offer is not as beneficial as previous plans, this may very well be our last chance at securing a deal with Lisbon over foreign investment. Accepting this deal would still allow for an American economic presence in Europe.
- However, should we accept, our presence will be severely limited by Lisbon's demands. Without proper privileges and investment rights, American businesses will only have a limited footprint in European markets.

options.text: Lisbon's got their deal. Let's go with their counteroffer.
This charade's gone on long enough. Stick with the original deal.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.15.title: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment
iberiawars_OFN_POR.15.description:
FROM: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
TO: The Council of Ministers
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment

We continue to discuss the second demand from the Americans concerning the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). They have insisted on special rights and privileges for private American businesses in Portuguese markets.

- The United States has rejected our counteroffer requesting fewer rights for American businesses in exchange for requiring less economic aid.
- Instead, the American delegation has stuck with their original deal. The United States requests that we accept their entire list of demands regarding what rights to grant private American firms and investors. In exchange, we will receive a large aid package to help with reconstruction efforts.
- However, the Ministry still has concerns about the implications this may have for local businesses and the extent of American influence in the Portuguese economy. We advise the Council of Ministers to be cautious.

- The United States stands firm on this issue. If we reject their proposal, we will be unable to move forward with the rest of the talks for the islands.
- Alternatively, the damages incurred by the Portuguese Civil War have left our economy in ruin. Any aid the Americans can grant would be welcomed.

options.text: The ends justify the means. We must accept the deal.
Stand up and leave. We have bent too far back for the Americans.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.16.title: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment
iberiawars_OFN_POR.16.description:
FROM: US State Department
TO: President [USA.GetLeader]
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment

We are continuing negotiations with the Portuguese government in Lisbon regarding the potential return of the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). Portugal has rejected our latest deal, and discussion regarding access to Portuguese markets for American investors have ended.

- We had offered Lisbon a reconstruction plan involving an economic aid package in exchange for rights for private American firms and investors.
- However, the Council of Ministers has dismissed this offer as an intrusion on Portuguese autonomy and that no privileges will be given to American businesses.
- Although the Portuguese economy had been left in ruin from the Portuguese Civil War, it is unlikely they will accept any economic aid from the American government or American businesses.

- The American delegation is considering withdrawing from the talks altogether. If Lisbon is unwilling to negotiate on the economy at all, even as they struggle to recover from the damage inflicted by the Portuguese Civil War, it may not bode well for future topics.
- Alternatively, if we do not wish to walk away from the negotiations, we can move on to our final topic.

options.text: We did not come all the way here to lose. Hopefully they'll be receptive to the next topic.
Walk out. If they don't want our help, so be it.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.17.title: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment
iberiawars_OFN_POR.17.description:
FROM: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
TO: The Council of Ministers
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment

We have received the second demand from the Americans concerning the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). They have requested an agreement concerning American foreign investment in Portugal.

- The United States has proposed limited economic aid to help reconstruction efforts for Portuguese infrastructure and industry. In exchange, we will need to grant American businesses preferential treatment for their businesses.
- The package itself is not large enough to cover our entire reconstruction; however, the Ministry is appreciative of the restraint the Americans show.
- As part of their preferential treatment, American businesses are expected to receive reduced tariffs, more tax breaks, and more lax customs processes.
- Many in the Ministry believe this to be an acceptable deal, but some warn the Council of Ministers that any offer like this may be capitulating our economic sovereignty to foreign powers.

- We can accept the deal as-is. Given the amount of infrastructure and industry that must be rebuilt, any amount of aid that the Americans can grant may be worth the preferential treatment we have to extend.
- We can also reject the deal. While the help is appreciated, the Americans may use this foot in the door to exploit our markets.

options.text: We do not need their business. We do not need their aid.
The terms could have been worse. Accept the deal.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.18.title: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment
iberiawars_OFN_POR.18.description:
FROM: US State Department
TO: President [USA.GetLeader]
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, II: Foreign Investment

We are continuing negotiations with the Portuguese government in Lisbon regarding the potential return of the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). Portugal has rejected our deal, and discussion regarding access to Portuguese markets for American investors has ended.

- We had offered Lisbon a reconstruction plan involving limited economic aid in exchange for preferential treatment towards American businesses.
- However, the Council of Ministers has dismissed this offer as an intrusion on Portuguese autonomy and that no special treatment, no matter how small, will be given to American businesses.
- We had set the bar as low as we could, and if the Portuguese government in Lisbon will not accept this offer, it is unlikely they will accept any help from us.

- The American delegation is considering withdrawing from the talks altogether. If Lisbon is unwilling to negotiate on the economy at all, even as they struggle to recover from the damage inflicted by the Portuguese Civil War, it may not bode well for future topics.
- Alternatively, if we do not wish to walk away from the negotiations, we can move on to our final topic.

options.text: We'll strike a better deal in our next round.
Withdraw. We're not spending another day in Lisbon.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.19.title: Azores and Madeira, III: Military Aid
iberiawars_OFN_POR.19.description:
FROM: US State Department
TO: President [USA.GetLeader]
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, III: Military Aid

We are continuing negotiations with the Portuguese government in Lisbon regarding the potential return of the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). We are opening up a new topic for discussion: military aid in exchange for oversight over Portuguese foreign policy.

- Portugal has been an integral part of the Iberian Union and Triumvirate alliance since the end of the Second World War. However, the Portuguese Civil War has left them politically isolated and militarily weakened.
- With much of their industry destroyed, Portugal's capacity to equip their army is limited. The government in Lisbon will appreciate military aid from America to bolster their armed forces.
- The Portuguese military high command could also benefit from the experience our American officers may provide via war games and training exercises.
- By backing Portugal's military, we will have an interest in directing Portugal's foreign policy to align with our own goals.
- Our biggest interest is securing friendly relations between Portugal and the United States. However, this may alienate Portugal from the rest of Europe, and Lisbon may not be appreciative of our influence over their foreign policy.

- We can offer Lisbon a significant amount of equipment, including armored vehicles and fighter planes, along with American officer liaisons to train the Portuguese military. In exchange, Portugal would be designated a strategic ally in Atlantic security.

options.text: To a partner across the Atlantic.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.20.title: Azores and Madeira, III: Military Aid
iberiawars_OFN_POR.20.description:
FROM: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
TO: The Council of Ministers
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, III: Military Aid

We have received the third demand from the Americans concerning the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). They have requested an agreement concerning American military aid to Portugal.

- In the wake of the Portuguese Civil War, our industry was crippled and thousands of soldiers were left dead. Lacking equipment and men, Portugal's security is threatened by foreign powers.
- Our nation is politically isolated, and without allies, Portugal may face pressure from our European neighbors.
- The United States has offered extensive military aid to bolster our army. The package includes shipments of armored vehicles and fighter planes. A more exhaustive list is attached to this document. The United States has also offered American personnel to help train our units.
- However, the United States requests oversight over our foreign policy. This includes friendlier relations between the United States and Portugal, and we would consider each other strategic allies across the Atlantic Ocean.
- The Ministry is concerned with the foreign policy restrictions, but agrees that the aid is crucial to maintaining our armed forces.

- We can choose to accept the plan as-is. The American aid outweighs the restrictions on our foreign policy.
- We may also negotiate the foreign policy part. In exchange for less aid, we can agree to stay away from European alliances.
- Alternatively, we may also outright reject all aid. Surrendering our foreign policy threatens our sovereignty.

options.text: Who the hell do the Americans think they are? Reject the aid.
Negotiate for fewer restrictions. We won't cozy up to Germany if they don't want us to.
Get those tanks and planes, and let's sign up with Uncle Sam.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.21.title: Azores and Madeira, III: Military Aid
iberiawars_OFN_POR.21.description:
FROM: US State Department
TO: President [USA.GetLeader]
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, III: Military Aid

We are continuing negotiations with the Portuguese government in Lisbon regarding the potential return of the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). We are continuing discussion regarding American military aid to Portugal.

- We previously proposed a military aid package involving large equipment shipments to bolster the Portuguese armed forces and military personnel to train Portuguese units.
- In exchange, we had requested oversight over Portuguese foreign policy, including the formation of a strategic alliance between the United States and Portugal.
- The Lisbon government has rejected this plan, claiming that the restrictions on foreign policy would violate its sovereignty.
- The Lisbon government has proposed a counteroffer and is willing to reduce the amount of military aid it receives while forgoing the American liaisons.
- In exchange, the Portuguese delegation promises they will stay away from European alliances. However, this is the only compromise they will make on foreign policy.

- We may accept this counteroffer. It will be less costly for the American government, while keeping Portugal away from rival factions.
- However, this does not accomplish our goal of keeping Portugal on friendly terms. We could push for our original deal one more time, but risk the Portuguese delegation withdrawing from the negotiations entirely.

options.text: We can take this as long as they don't join our enemies.
We're not just handing out guns here. We need more than assurances.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.22.title: Azores and Madeira, III: Military Aid
iberiawars_OFN_POR.22.description:
FROM: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
TO: The Council of Ministers
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, III: Military Aid

We have received the third demand from the Americans concerning the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). They have insisted on American oversight over Portuguese foreign policy in exchange for military aid.

- The United States has rejected our counteroffer requesting less military aid in exchange for more freedom over our foreign policy.
- The American delegation has stuck with their original deal. Our assurances to stay away from European alliances were not enough, and they have requested Portugal to join the United States as a strategic ally in Atlantic security in exchange for military aid.
- However, the Ministry is still concerned about the implications this alliance may have on our European relations. Although we would receive a substantial amount of military aid, we may risk alienation from most of Europe. We advise the Council of Ministers to be cautious.

- The United States is unwilling to compromise on this issue. Without any compromise, we may withdraw from the talks entirely.
- Alternatively, the aid would substantially strengthen our military. We may as well accept the original deal to end talks on a positive note.
- However, the restrictions may be too much. We can also agree to disagree and move on with the talks.

options.text: Take the original deal. Friendly relations with America shouldn't be a bad thing.
Agree to disagree. Let's not get bogged down on this issue.
Leave. Do they seriously think they can make us their puppet?

iberiawars_OFN_POR.23.title: Azores and Madeira, III: Military Aid
iberiawars_OFN_POR.23.description:
FROM: US State Department
TO: President [USA.GetLeader]
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, III: Military Aid

We are continuing negotiations with the Portuguese government in Lisbon regarding the potential return of the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). We are continuing discussion regarding American military aid to Portugal.

- We previously proposed a military aid package involving large equipment shipments to bolster the Portuguese armed forces and military personnel to train Portuguese units.
- In exchange, we had requested oversight over Portuguese foreign policy, including a strategic alliance between the United States and Portugal.
- The Lisbon government has rejected this plan, claiming that the restrictions on foreign policy would violate its sovereignty. They are unwilling to negotiate anything that compromises their foreign policy and reject our military aid package.
- Without a deal on Portugal's foreign policy, we run the risk of Portugal aligning themselves with hostile nations.

- We may accept their wishes and concede control over Portugal's foreign policy. This will mean we do not have to undergo the burden of propping up Portugal's weakened military.
- Alternatively, we could lower the restrictions and simply request Portugal to stay away from any European alliances, in exchange for a smaller military aid package.

options.text: Lower the deal. We have not come this far to give up.
Let's just accept and finish the talks. I'm starting to get homesick.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.24.title: Azores and Madeira, III: Military Aid
iberiawars_OFN_POR.24.description:
FROM: US State Department
TO: President [USA.GetLeader]
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, III: Military Aid

We are continuing negotiations with the Portuguese government in Lisbon regarding the potential return of the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). We are continuing discussion regarding American military aid to Portugal.

- We previously proposed a limited military aid package involving equipment shipments to strengthen the Portuguese armed forces.
- In exchange, we had requested they stay away from aligning with any European alliances.
- The Lisbon government has rejected this proposal, claiming that it will not allow any American influence on Portuguese foreign policy, no matter how small.
- Despite the disagreements, Portugal has not walked out of the negotiations. Seeing that both sides cannot be reconciled on their positions, the Portuguese delegation has offered to drop the issue and conclude the talks.

options.text: Then we move forward.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.25.title: Azores and Madeira, III: Military Aid
iberiawars_OFN_POR.25.description:
FROM: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
TO: The Council of Ministers
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, III: Military Aid

We have received the third demand from the Americans concerning the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands"). They have proposed a counteroffer involving less military aid for fewer restrictions on Portuguese foreign policy.

- Initially, we had rejected all American military aid in exchange that they would not compromise our foreign policy in any way.
- However, the United States has proposed a counteroffer. In exchange for a small amount of military aid through equipment shipments, they request that we stay away from European alliances.
- The Ministry is still concerned about America's influence on Portugal's foreign policy, no matter how small. A deal like this will alienate us from our European neighbors.
- Nevertheless, this offer is much more palatable, and the military aid would still be extremely helpful in rearming our military forces.

- Despite that, we may reject this deal and avoid any American interference in our foreign policy matters.
- Still, the military aid is extremely helpful and needed at a time when our military does not have the resources to properly arm itself. American influence on our foreign policy will be minimal.

options.text: They compromised. Now we compromise and accept their deal.
Our initial statement still holds. No American will dictate Portuguese foreign matters. They'll understand.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.26.title: Azores and Madeira, IV: The Atlantic Compromise
iberiawars_OFN_POR.26.description:
The flurry of camera flashes floods the stage as the Portuguese delegate walks to a podium flanked by the [?event_target:IBR_portuguese_winner.GetNameDef] and the American flag. The crowd is hushed into whispers as the spokesperson lightly taps on the microphone.

His words are brief, yet they drag the entire room with them.

"Washington," the spokesperson announces, "has formally recognized the [?event_target:IBR_portuguese_winner.GetNameDef]'s sovereignty over our former archipelagos of Azores and Madeira.

"They have demanded that the illegitimate Portuguese Confederation capitulate to us. Within twenty-four hours, our troops will have liberated the islands.

"Efforts to restore administrative control over the islands are already underway."

When pressed for additional details regarding the terms of the agreement, the delegate could only offer a measured smile.

As the last journalists filed out with unanswered questions, the spokesperson remained alone with his thoughts. Weeks of negotiations, choosing every word so precisely, now felt so distant.

How much had been given up, how much had remained intact, didn't matter for the newly reborn nation. In the ashes that it had risen from, it endured another trial amidst the greatest power in the New World.

But Portugal was no stranger to dealing across the Atlantic.

options.text: So we find ourselves drawing lines across the ocean again.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.27.title: Azores and Madeira, IV: The Atlantic Compromise
iberiawars_OFN_POR.27.description:
FROM: US State Department
TO: President [USA.GetLeader]
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, IV: Conclusion of Negotiations

We report that negotiations with the Portuguese government in Lisbon regarding the potential return of the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands") have concluded successfully. A common understanding has been achieved between the two nations, establishing a mutually acceptable framework going forward.

In accordance with the outcome:

- The United States has formally withdrawn all political and material support from the illegitimate Portuguese Confederation.
- The United States has sent an ultimatum to the illegitimate Portuguese Confederation on the islands, requesting that they peacefully surrender to the [?event_target:IBR_portuguese_winner.GetNameDef].
- The [?event_target:IBR_portuguese_winner.GetNameDef] is recognized as the sole sovereign authority over the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira.
- Existing arrangements reached during the course of the negotiations will govern future relations regarding the islands and both nations.

This matter is considered closed.

options.text: The Atlantic is settled.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.28.title: Azores and Madeira, IV: The Atlantic Deadlock
iberiawars_OFN_POR.28.description:
The flurry of camera flashes floods the stage as the Portuguese delegate walks to a podium flanked by only the [?event_target:IBR_portuguese_winner.GetNameDef]'s flag. The crowd is hushed into whispers as the spokesperson lightly taps on the microphone.

His words are brief, yet they drag the entire room with them.

"Washington," the spokesperson announces, "has refused to respect Portuguese sovereignty in key matters of national importance. Consequently... the negotiations have collapsed.

"The Americans have refused to recognize our claim over the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira. They have opened up diplomatic channels with the illegitimate Portuguese Confederation that still occupies our islands.

"Despite this setback, Portugal remains resolute. We are still looking to secure the islands under our control... even through other means."

When pressed for additional details regarding the next possible steps, the delegate could only drag his feet off the stage.

As the last journalists filed out with unanswered questions, the spokesperson lingered alone with his thoughts. His mind traced the long nights he spent over the diplomatic talks. Every careful word, every concession made, all lost to the Atlantic's crashing waves.

Though it didn't matter how much could have been gained for the newly reborn nation. In the ashes that it had risen from, it endured another trial amidst the greatest power in the New World.

But the New World would no longer bow to Portugal's treaties.

options.text: But we still have contingencies.

iberiawars_OFN_POR.29.title: Azores and Madeira, IV: The Atlantic Deadlock
iberiawars_OFN_POR.29.description:
FROM: US State Department
TO: President [USA.GetLeader]
SUBJECT: Azores and Madeira, IV: Breakdown of Negotiations

We report that negotiations with the Portuguese government in Lisbon regarding the potential return of the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira ("the islands") have concluded without agreement. Talks ultimately broke down due to Lisbon's unwillingness to compromise on outstanding issues.

In accordance with the outcome:

- The United States does not recognize the [?event_target:IBR_portuguese_winner.GetNameDef]'s sovereignty over the archipelagos of Azores and Madeira.
- All prior understandings reached during the course of the negotiations have been considered void.
- Diplomatic channels with the Portuguese Confederation have been opened, including a potential operation against the mainland. This plan is now under active consideration.

This matter remains unresolved.

options.text: We have contingencies.

iberiawars_OFN_SPA.1.title: The Matter of Portugal
iberiawars_OFN_SPA.1.description:
The decision has been made, at the highest levels, to commence negotiations with the Americans as to the status of Portugal and our current occupation of it. The particulars of the summit are being established, but it is happening and we must ensure that we remain in the strongest possible position.

It is clear that the Americans wish for the government of the Portuguese Confederation, recognized by them as the legitimate Portuguese government but isolated to the Azores following the fall of Lisbon, to return to the continent. The potential ramifications of such a return are significant, as are the concessions that we may be able to demand for allowing it.

In any case, it will be our task to ensure that the State benefits to the greatest degree possible while also minimizing any potential OFN presence in the country. The Portuguese occupation may be ruinously expensive, yes, but we must not be distracted by that. We will not, under any circumstances, allow Portugal to become a staging ground for the OFN to pressure Iberia.

options.text: Continue preparations for the summit.

iberiawars_OFN_SPA.2.title: The Question of Portugal
iberiawars_OFN_SPA.2.description:
We have just received word that the Spanish government has accepted our offer of a summit on the future of continental Portugal - and the potential of the Confederation's return to it.

The government of the Confederation, currently in the Azores, desperately wishes to return to the metropole currently occupied by the Spaniards. Ordinarily, there would be no reason why this would even be entertained but Spain is fragile and under immense resource strain with their occupation. The occupation of Portugal is ruinously expensive - they simply cannot afford it - that gives us a window.

No doubt Spain will be watchful as to the conditions, especially any regarding future OFN presence within any potential Portuguese state, and we will have to compensate them greatly in one fashion or another. However, the rewards of securing Portuguese return cannot be understated in moral, political, or military terms. Securing Portugal would give us a foothold on the European continent itself - something worth nearly any price. We must work towards success.

options.text: Prepare the delegation.

iberiawars_OFN_SPA.3.title: Preparing the Offers
iberiawars_OFN_SPA.3.description:
As the summit nears, it is clear that the one issue that will dominate all discussions, regardless of the number of technicalities to be worked out, is the position of any Portuguese state within the OFN and what that means for the military positioning and influence of the related powers.

Naturally, it would be our goal for the OFN to be strongly positioned in a future Portugal, offering a stronghold on continental Europe. With Portugal we would be able to flex our muscles on the doorstep of the Reich and the Mediterranean. Just as naturally, the Spanish goal is to minimize this and oppose the Confederation's alignment within the OFN while extracting maximum economic considerations. Understandable, given the Spanish distrust of foreign powers given their weakened position

As such, we must ensure that we have multiple options to present, allowing for our delegation to present whichever outcome they think will work best in the moment. We must not be caught out of position if these negotiations are to succeed.

options.text: Begin drafting the options.

iberiawars_OFN_SPA.4.title: The OFN in Portugal?
iberiawars_OFN_SPA.4.description:
The Americans want the Portuguese Confederation to be aligned with them and have OFN personnel stationed there. Desiring OFN troops, rather than just American troops, paints their wider designs clearly; they want Portugal absorbed into their alliance and used as a soldier in their conflicts - not just an aligned partner. Obviously we can't accept such intrusions on our borders. The question is, however, how much are we willing to let the OFN do?

As expected, the Americans wish for the Portuguese Confederation, once returned to Portugal proper from exile, to be aligned with the OFN - and even have OFN personnel stationed there. This represents an unacceptable intrusion in its unrestricted form.

We cannot have OFN forces stationed in Portugal - it is undeniable that they would use it as a staging ground for destabilization and, potentially, future subversion of the Spanish state. However, there will need to be some level of compromise for a deal to be reached, and we can certainly make the Americans pay for it.

Our representatives, therefore, are asking for what potential OFN presence we may be willing to tolerate. What should our answer be?

options.text: This must succeed. Allow OFN observers.
We can compromise. Allow OFN diplomats.
No compromise. No OFN personnel at all.

iberiawars_OFN_SPA.5.title: The Offer: Cash for Observers?
iberiawars_OFN_SPA.5.description:
Our representatives at the summit have returned to us a most interesting and unexpected offer on the part of the Spaniards regarding Portugal. They implore us to consider it, given the tense atmosphere regarding the Portuguese question.

Fundamentally, Spain will capitulate on the matter of OFN Observer status for Portugal, and even permit OFN personnel and resources on Portugal's Atlantic holdings. This would be a major accomplishment both for the OFN and four our efforts in expanding it, and given the obvious antipathy the Spanish have towards it, likely the absolute most that they would be willing to tolerate.

In exchange? Money. An extremely favorable economic agreement, which would be of near-incalculable help in supporting their almost moribund economy. The cost is significant, but not immensely so - and the rewards immense.

This is certainly the best offer that we are going to get - how should our representatives be instructed to reply?

options.text: It's worth the cost. Accept the offer.
Unacceptable. Reject the offer.

iberiawars_OFN_SPA.6.title: The Line: No OFN Personnel
iberiawars_OFN_SPA.6.description:
Our representatives at the negotiations concerning Portugal have returned with the Spanish position, and it is both clear and less acceptable than was hoped.

Fundamentally, the Spaniards accept that Portugal will be granted OFN Observer status, recognizing that inevitability. But they will not permit OFN personnel and resources to be stationed anywhere on Portuguese territories. Certainly not the metropole, and not on Atlantic holdings, either - though this second exclusion was much less strongly voiced.

Our representatives thus suggest that there is the potential to obtain agreement for physical OFN presence in those Atlantic holdings - if we are willing to pay for it through a very favorable economic agreement. We could do so, or we could accept the win on Observer status and move on.

How should the diplomats be instructed?

options.text: Propose the compromise. See what we can get.
Not worth it. Move on to the next issue.

iberiawars_OFN_SPA.7.title: The Response: Cash for Observers?
iberiawars_OFN_SPA.7.description:
The OFN delegation has returned to us, following our last round of talks, with a counterproposal regarding the potential of OFN personnel on Portuguese territory.

Our agents there were clear that we would not, and never would, agree to OFN personnel present on the Portuguese mainland - but arguments against their presence on the Atlantic holdings are much less vehement. The OFN has clearly realized this, and are proposing that we accept that presence in exchange for an extremely favorable economic agreement between ourselves and the United States.

This would be extremely impactful, potentially driving considerable economic growth. There will of course be dissent on the presence of any OFN personnel at all, but those voices can be drowned out, if we wish to do so.

How should our delegation respond?

options.text: That is acceptable. Accept the offer.
No. We must hold the line. Reject the offer.

iberiawars_OFN_SPA.8.title: The Line, Held Firm
iberiawars_OFN_SPA.8.description:
A quick response from the continuing talks on Portugal. And not one that we hoped to receive.

The Spanish have flatly rejected the offered compromise - OFN presence in Portugal's Atlantic holdings in exchange for an economic agreement. They simply will not accept anything beyond Portugal acquiring OFN Observer status, and have refused to negotiate further.

This is clearly a red line for them, and our delegates do not think any further movement is possible here, unless we wish to torpedo the entire summit and walk away from any deal at all.

options.text: Understood. Accept the line and move on.
Then we will. Walk away.

iberiawars_OFN_SPA.9.title: The Neutrality Demand
iberiawars_OFN_SPA.9.description:
We have received a response from our delegates, and that response is not what was desired. The Spanish have made it clear that Portugal must remain strictly neutral with regards to the OFN.

This is of course a significant blow for us, compromising many plans intended to leverage a Portuguese OFN toehold on the Continent. Although attempts were made to find positions for compromise, all were (at least at this stage) flatly rejected by the Spanish representatives, indicating instructions from their own government as to this particular.

It is considered unlikely that there is further space for movement on this topic. We can certainly try, of course, but we must choose whether to do so, accept the current state and move forward, or walk away from the conference entirely in response.

How should our representatives be instructed?

options.text: We must try again. Reiterate our desire to negotiate.
We must be realistic. Accept it and move on.
Unacceptable. Terminate negotiations and walk out.

iberiawars_OFN_SPA.10.title: Yet Another Attempt
iberiawars_OFN_SPA.10.description:
The Americans continue to push for OFN involvement in any future Portuguese state, over - and seemingly in spite of - our refusals to just that desire.

Yet another compromise has been offered to us, in the hopes of finally finding something palatable to our future strategic considerations. They of course wish for Portugal to be formally aligned with the OFN, of course, but should we accept that they are willing to drop requests for the presence of personnel entirely.

It is a tiring response in light of positions, indeed, but considering it is not without merit. By far the biggest threat to our future state is OFN troop presence in Portugal, but if that is surrendered, and we accept simple alignment - which is far less dangerous - we remove the threat while keeping space for future gains on our part.

It is a decision, to be sure - what should the response be?

options.text: We can accept alignment. But no troops.
No. Not even alignment is acceptable.

iberiawars_OFN_SPA.11.title: The Final Rejection
iberiawars_OFN_SPA.11.description:
We tried, but there was no room for maneuver. The Spanish have rejected the proposal for even OFN alignment for Portugal, let alone any other involvement.

It is obvious that they will not budge on this. They have made the decision to brook no OFN presence on their border, and are bent on ensuring total Portuguese neutrality. There is no future possibility for compromise, and this is clearly the end of the issue as far as they are concerned. We must choose whether it is the end of the issue for ourselves as well.

How should we respond?

options.text: We must accept this. Move on.
Unacceptable. Walk out of the talks.

iberiawars_OFN_SPA.12.title: The Question of the Military
iberiawars_OFN_SPA.12.description:
As the conference progresses, the second issue of major tension between ourselves and the Spanish concerns the future of any Portuguese armed forces.

Spain's position is clear - they wish for heavy restrictions on the composition of a potential Portuguese military, and further demand to be allowed to perform inspections in order to ensure that such restrictions are enforced. This is obviously not desirable to ourselves, the OFN, or even the Portuguese people themselves, who naturally deserve a capable defense. We must find a compromise.

Several options have been presented. We can enshrine a Portuguese commitment to self-defense only in any agreement, providing assurances against attack - which might allow us to propose removing inspections entirely. Or, if we do not wish to hamstring Portugal so, we can propose a third-party observer, from a neutral state or other organization.

How should our delegates be instructed to open the discussion on this topic?

options.text: We will give assurances that Portugal will not attack.
We will offer a third-party overseer.

iberiawars_OFN_SPA.13.title: The Americans Dismiss Portuguese Military Restrictions
iberiawars_OFN_SPA.13.description:
The American negotiators have come back to us, denying our request for oversight over the formation of new Portuguese armed forces. They claim that such a body would constitute a gross violation of Portuguese sovereignty; something that could have grave consequences for us both if it fosters resentment, thinly hinting at the aftermath of the First World War. Instead, they offer a US guarantee that the future Portuguese government would never attempt offensive action against us, using their own oversight as well as constitutional commitments in the new nation to only pursue self-defence.

Some in our delegation believe this to be reasonable enough. The long-term purpose of such an overseeing body remains an open question, especially as we continue to be forced to fight partisans and rebuild our own country. The Portuguese are already broken and the Americans will understand the OFN cannot violently expand without the Reich intervening. This is all without mentioning our superior industry to Portugal. So long as we keep an eye on them. there should be no cause for concern.

At least, that's what our more dovish delegates believe. Other delegates have already decried this as servility, claiming that if left unchecked Portugal could serve as a backdoor for American interests, capital or even military force to penetrate our borders. Further, should the Reich even think we have become a stooge to the Yanquis would they hesitate to interfere? Would America help us despite our service? We, they say, are being used and we must make it clear that we see any form of an uninhibited Portuguese military as a grave security threat on which we will not retreat.

options.text: This could also get us some goodwill from Uncle Sam...
We beat American stooges in Spain itself - we will not let them regroup in Portugal.

iberiawars_OFN_SPA.14.title: The Spanish Agree to Drop Portuguese Military Restrictions
iberiawars_OFN_SPA.14.description:
After a few days of debate and consultation with Madrid, the Spanish delegates have returned to us with an answer - and it is cautiously affirmative. They say that they are willing to let the issue of Portuguese military restrictions drop, but they have also made it abundantly clear that they hold us responsible to hold Lisbon on a tight leash - they will not hold back in their response to any provocation from the Portuguese side of the border and will see us as directly responsible.

Our sources in the Portuguese Confederation have informed us that they do not expect the new government to attempt any provocation, not to mention an outright attack, on the Spanish at any point in the foreseeable future - very few in Portugal wish to return to the days of the Union, and even if they did, the government will have to spend years rebuilding Portugal's devastated infrastructure and shattered institutions before they could even think about invading the much larger Spain.

That being the case, it seems that this issue has been mostly resolved. Some in our sources consider it likely that the Spanish will attempt some sort of provocation on the Portuguese border at some point - but the Spanish are just as battered as the Portuguese, and it seems that Iberia should be able to know a few years of peace at the very least.

options.text: On to the next issue!

iberiawars_OFN_SPA.15.title: The Spanish Insist on Portuguese Military Restrictions
iberiawars_OFN_SPA.15.description:
Despite our numerous attempts to placate the Spanish, telling them that the Portuguese government would not have the will or the capacity to attempt any serious provocation, let alone an invasion, as well as offering them our guarantee to hold back the Portuguese even in the off chance that they get the idea of crossing the border, the Spanish have refused to budge. They have informed us in no uncertain terms that they will not acquiesce to any restoration of the Portuguese state that does not provide them with robust means of enforcing strict military restrictions on it.

Our negotiators are quite dismayed by this development. While not our preferred contestant to come out of the wreckage of the union, many in the State Department had hoped the regime could be reasonable - apparently, this is not the case. We do, however, still have a few possible choices to make.

Some delegates propose simply acquiescing to the Spanish demands - unsatisfying as it may be, it will help smooth things over with the regime and enable us to work with them in the future, pragmatically if not cordially. Others suggest we agree to the Spanish demands in principle, but demand that a more impartial third party oversee the maintenance of the military restrictions, hopefully without undermining the viability of the Portuguese state. However, a growing clique of State Department officials are now openly calling for us to walk out of the negotiations - if the Spanish believe that they can force us to bend to their every whim, they will have to learn their lesson the hard way.
